title.zh: 卷一百九十二 列傳第一百十七 忠義中
title.raw: 卷一百九十二 列傳第一百十七 忠義中 Volume 192 Biographies 117: Loyalty and Righteousness 2

sentences.zh: 忠義中顏杲卿春卿賈循隱林張巡許遠南霽雲雷萬春姚訚

translations.literal: Loyalty and Righteousness (middle): Yan Gaoqing, Chunqing, Jia Xun, Yin Lin, Zhang Xun, Xu Yuan, Nan Jiyun, Lei Wanchun, Yao Yan
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty and Righteousness (continued): biographies of Yan Gaoqing, Chunqing, Jia Xun, Yin Lin, Zhang Xun, Xu Yuan, Nan Jiyun, Lei Wanchun, and Yao Yan

sentences.zh: 顏杲卿字昕，與真卿同五世祖，以文儒世家。

translations.literal: Yan Gaoqing, courtesy name Xin, shared a fifth-generation ancestor with Zhenqing; his was a family renowned for literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Gaoqing, whose courtesy name was Xin, was a fifth-generation kinsman of Yan Zhenqing and came from a long line of scholars and officials.

sentences.zh: 父元孫，有名垂拱間，為濠州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yuansun was famous in the Chonggong era and served as prefect of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuansun won renown during the Chonggong years and held office as prefect of Hao.

sentences.zh: 杲卿以蔭調遂州司法參軍。

translations.literal: Gaoqing entered office by yin privilege as judicial assistant in Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing received his first appointment through hereditary privilege as judicial assistant in Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 性剛正，蒞事明濟。

translations.literal: His nature was stern and upright; in conducting affairs he was clear and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: He was stern and upright by nature, and in office he handled matters with clarity and decisiveness.

sentences.zh: 嘗為刺史詰讓，正色別白，不為屈。

translations.literal: Once when a prefect rebuked him, he explained matters with a stern expression and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: When a prefect once rebuked him, he answered with a grave face, setting right and wrong plainly, and would not be cowed.

sentences.zh: 開元中，與兄春卿、弟曜卿並以書判超等，吏部侍郎席豫咨嗟推伏。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era he, his elder brother Chunqing, and his younger brother Yaoging all passed the shupan examination with superior marks; Vice Minister of Personnel Xi Yu sighed in admiration and commended them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign, he and his brothers Chunqing and Yaoging all earned top marks in the document-examination circuit, and Xi Yu, vice minister of personnel, marveled and spoke highly of them.

sentences.zh: 再以最遷范陽戶曹參軍。

translations.literal: Again by highest rank he was promoted to revenue assistant in Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again, on highest evaluation, to revenue assistant in Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 安祿山聞其名，表為營田判官，假常山太守。

translations.literal: An Lushan heard his name and memorialized him as agricultural colony judge, with acting appointment as prefect of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan, hearing of his reputation, recommended him as agricultural colony judge and gave him acting rank as prefect of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 祿山反，杲卿及長史袁履謙謁於道，賜杲卿紫袍，履謙緋袍，令與假子李欽湊以兵七千屯土門。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, Gaoqing and Chief Administrator Yuan Lüqian met him on the road; Lushan granted Gaoqing a purple robe and Lüqian a scarlet robe, and ordered them with his foster son Li Qincou to station seven thousand troops at Tumen.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rose in rebellion, Gaoqing and Chief Administrator Yuan Lüqian went out to meet him on the road. Lushan gave Gaoqing a purple robe and Lüqian a scarlet one, then sent them with his foster son Li Qincou and seven thousand men to hold Tumen Pass.

sentences.zh: 杲卿指所賜衣謂履謙曰：「與公何為著此？」

translations.literal: Gaoqing pointed at the robes they had been given and said to Lüqian, "Why are you wearing these?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing pointed at the robes they had been given and said to Lüqian, "Why in the world are you wearing these?"

sentences.zh: 履謙悟，乃與真定令賈深、內丘令張通幽定謀圖賊。

translations.literal: Lüqian understood; then together with Zhending magistrate Jia Shen and Neiqiu magistrate Zhang Tongyou they plotted against the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Lüqian took his meaning at once. He joined Zhending magistrate Jia Shen and Neiqiu magistrate Zhang Tongyou in a secret plan to strike at the rebels.

sentences.zh: 杲卿稱疾不視事，使子泉明往返計議，陰結太原尹王承業為應，使平盧節度副使賈循取幽州。

translations.literal: Gaoqing feigned illness and did not attend to business, sending his son Quanming back and forth to deliberate; he secretly joined with Taiyuan intendant Wang Chengye for support and had Pinglu deputy commissioner Jia Xun take Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing pleaded illness and stayed out of office, while his son Quanming shuttled back and forth carrying their plans. In secret he aligned with Taiyuan intendant Wang Chengye and ordered Pinglu deputy commissioner Jia Xun to seize Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 謀泄，祿山殺循，以向潤客、牛廷玠守。

translations.literal: The plot leaked; Lushan killed Xun and put Xiang Runkè and Niu Tingjie in charge of the defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, Lushan executed Xun and placed Xiang Runkè and Niu Tingjie in command of the city.

sentences.zh: 杲卿陽不事事，委政履謙，潛召處士權渙、郭仲邕定策。

translations.literal: Gaoqing outwardly attended to nothing, entrusted government to Lüqian, and secretly summoned recluses Quan Huan and Guo Zhongyong to fix strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing pretended to take no part in affairs, leaving government to Lüqian while quietly summoning the recluses Quan Huan and Guo Zhongyong to shape their strategy.

sentences.zh: 時真卿在平原，素聞賊逆謀，陰養死士為拒守計。

translations.literal: At that time Zhenqing was in Pingyuan; he had long heard of the rebels' treasonous designs and secretly kept devoted fighters for a plan of resistance and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing was then in Pingyuan. He had long known of the rebels' designs and was quietly training loyal men to hold the region.

sentences.zh: 李憕等死，賊使段子光傳首徇諸郡，真卿斬子光，遣甥盧逖至常山約起兵，斷賊北道。

translations.literal: After Li Qin and others died, the rebels sent Duan Ziguang to parade their heads through the commanderies; Zhenqing executed Ziguang, sent his nephew Lu Ti to Changshan to arrange a rising, and cut the rebels' northern route.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Qin and his fellows were killed, the rebels sent Duan Ziguang to display their heads in the commanderies. Zhenqing beheaded Ziguang, sent his nephew Lu Ti to Changshan to arrange a rising, and aimed to sever the rebels' northern line of advance.

sentences.zh: 杲卿大喜，以為兵掎角可挫賊西鋒。

translations.literal: Gaoqing was greatly pleased, thinking that with forces pincering each other they could blunt the rebels' western thrust.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing was overjoyed, believing that with allied forces striking from two sides they could blunt the rebels' drive westward.

sentences.zh: 乃矯賊命召欽湊計事，欽湊夜還，杲卿辭城門不可夜開，舍之外郵；

translations.literal: Then they forged rebel orders summoning Qincou to discuss affairs; Qincou returned at night, and Gaoqing pleaded that the city gates could not be opened at night and lodged him at the outer postal station;
translations.idiomatic: They forged rebel orders summoning Qincou for consultation. When he returned at night, Gaoqing refused to open the gates after dark and put him up at the outer relay station;

sentences.zh: 使履謙及參軍馮虔、郡豪翟萬德等數人飲勞，既醉，斬之，並殺其將潘惟慎，賊黨殲，投屍滹沱水。

translations.literal: He had Lüqian and Assistant Feng Qian, the county stalwart Zhai Wande, and several others entertain and toast him; once drunk they beheaded him, also killed his general Pan Weishèn, wiped out the rebel party, and threw the bodies into the Hutuo River.
translations.idiomatic: Lüqian, Assistant Feng Qian, the local leader Zhai Wande, and several others were sent to wine and feast him. Once he was drunk they cut off his head, killed his officer Pan Weishèn as well, destroyed the rebel band, and cast the corpses into the Hutuo.

sentences.zh: 履謙以首示杲卿，則喜且泣。

translations.literal: Lüqian showed the head to Gaoqing, who then rejoiced and wept.
translations.idiomatic: When Lüqian showed him the head, Gaoqing wept for joy.

sentences.zh: 先是，祿山遣將高邈召兵范陽未還，杲卿使城尉崔安石圖之。

translations.literal: Earlier Lushan had sent the general Gao Miao to summon troops in Fanyang and he had not yet returned; Gaoqing had the city commandant Cui Anshi plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Lushan had sent General Gao Miao to raise troops in Fanyang, and he had not yet returned. Gaoqing set the city commandant Cui Anshi to take him.

sentences.zh: 邈至滿城，虔、萬德皆會傳舍，安石紿以置酒，邈舍馬，虔叱吏縛之。

translations.literal: When Miao reached Mancheng, Qian and Wande both met at the relay inn; Anshi deceived him with an offer of wine, Miao dismounted, and Qian shouted for clerks to bind him.
translations.idiomatic: Miao reached Mancheng, where Qian and Wande waited at the relay inn. Anshi lured him in with wine; as soon as Miao dismounted, Qian ordered the clerks to seize him.

sentences.zh: 而賊將何千年自趙來，虔亦執之。

translations.literal: When the rebel general He Qiannian came from Zhao, Qian seized him as well.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel general He Qiannian arrived from Zhao, Qian captured him too.

sentences.zh: 日未中，送二賊。

translations.literal: Before midday they sent off the two rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Before noon they had both rebels on their way.

sentences.zh: 杲卿乃遣萬德、深、通幽傳欽湊首，械兩賊送京師，與泉明偕。

translations.literal: Gaoqing then sent Wande, Shen, and Tongyou to carry Qincou's head, put the two rebels in fetters and send them to the capital, and Quanming went with them.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing sent Wande, Shen, and Tongyou ahead with Qincou's head while the two captives were shackled and sent to the capital with Quanming escorting them.

sentences.zh: 至太原，王承業欲自以為功，厚遣泉明還，陰令壯士翟喬賊於路。

translations.literal: At Taiyuan, Wang Chengye wished to claim the merit himself, sent Quanming back with rich gifts, and secretly ordered the stalwart Zhai Qiao to rob the prisoners on the road.
translations.idiomatic: At Taiyuan, Wang Chengye wanted the credit for himself. He sent Quanming back with lavish rewards and secretly told the warrior Zhai Qiao to waylay the prisoners on the road.

sentences.zh: 喬不平，告之故，乃免。

translations.literal: Qiao was indignant, told them the reason, and they were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao, offended by the order, revealed the plot, and the prisoners were spared.

sentences.zh: 玄宗擢承業大將軍，送吏皆被賞。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong promoted Chengye to great general; all the escorting officials were rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong promoted Chengye to great general, while every man in the escort received a reward.

sentences.zh: 已而事顯，乃拜杲卿衛尉卿兼御史中丞，履謙常山太守，深司馬。

translations.literal: Soon the affair became known; then Gaoqing was appointed Minister of the Court for the Imperial Insignia and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Lüqian prefect of Changshan, and Shen military aide.
translations.idiomatic: When word of their deeds spread, Gaoqing was made Minister of the Court for the Imperial Insignia and concurrent censor-in-chief, Lüqian was confirmed as prefect of Changshan, and Shen became military aide.

sentences.zh: 即傳檄河北，言王師二十萬入土門，遣郭仲邕領百騎為先鋒，馳而南，曳柴揚塵，望者謂大軍至。

translations.literal: At once he issued proclamations through Hebei saying two hundred thousand imperial troops had entered Tumen, sent Guo Zhongyong at the head of a hundred horsemen as vanguard, galloped south dragging brush to raise dust, and onlookers thought the great army had arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He at once sent proclamations across Hebei claiming two hundred thousand imperial troops had entered Tumen Pass. Guo Zhongyong led a hundred horsemen south as vanguard, dragging brush to raise dust so that watchers believed a great army was upon them.

sentences.zh: 日中，傳數百里。

translations.literal: By midday the report had spread several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: By midday the rumor had raced hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 賊張獻誠方圍饒陽，棄甲走。

translations.literal: The rebel Zhang Xiancheng was then besieging Raoyang and cast off his armor and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Zhang Xiancheng, who was besieging Raoyang, threw down his armor and fled.

sentences.zh: 於是趙、鉅鹿、廣平、河間並斬偽刺史，傳首常山。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhao, Julu, Guangping, and Hejian all beheaded the false prefects and sent the heads to Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Then Zhao, Julu, Guangping, and Hejian all executed the rebel prefects and sent their heads to Changshan.

sentences.zh: 而樂安、博陵、上谷、文安、信都、魏、鄴諸郡皆自固。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the commanderies of Le'an, Boling, Shanggu, Wen'an, Xindu, Wei, and Ye all fortified themselves on their own.
translations.idiomatic: The commanderies of Le'an, Boling, Shanggu, Wen'an, Xindu, Wei, and Ye likewise sealed their walls and held out on their own.

sentences.zh: 杲卿兄弟兵大振。

translations.literal: The forces of Gaoqing and his brothers greatly revived.
translations.idiomatic: The armies of Gaoqing and his kinsmen surged to new strength.

sentences.zh: 祿山至陜，聞兵興，大懼。

translations.literal: Lushan reached Shan and, hearing that troops had risen, was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan reached Shanzhou and heard that armies had risen against him, he was badly shaken.

sentences.zh: 使史思明等率平盧兵度河攻常山，蔡希德自懷會師。

translations.literal: He sent Shi Siming and others to lead Pinglu troops across the river to attack Changshan, while Cai Xide joined forces from Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Shi Siming and others with Pinglu troops across the river against Changshan, while Cai Xide marched up from Huai to join them.

sentences.zh: 不涉旬，賊急攻城。

translations.literal: Within less than ten days the rebels pressed the assault on the city.
translations.idiomatic: In less than ten days the rebels were pressing the city hard.

sentences.zh: 兵少，未及為守計，求救於河東，承業前已攘殺賊功，兵不出。

translations.literal: Their troops were few and they had not yet made plans for defense; they begged aid from Hedong, but Chengye had already seized credit for killing the rebels and would not send troops.
translations.idiomatic: They had too few men and no time to prepare a proper defense. They pleaded for help from Hedong, but Chengye, who had already claimed the rebels' heads as his own merit, refused to march.

sentences.zh: 杲卿晝夜戰，井竭，糧、矢盡，六日而陷，與履謙同執。

translations.literal: Gaoqing fought day and night; the wells ran dry, grain and arrows were exhausted, and on the sixth day the city fell; he and Lüqian were seized together.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing fought without rest day and night until the wells ran dry and food and arrows were gone. On the sixth day the city fell, and he and Lüqian were taken together.

sentences.zh: 賊脅使降，不應。

translations.literal: The rebels threatened him to make him submit; he would not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pressed him to surrender; he would not yield.

sentences.zh: 取少子季明加刃頸上曰：「降我，當活而子。」

translations.literal: They took his younger son Jiming, set a blade to his neck, and said, "Submit to me and I will let your son live."
translations.idiomatic: They seized his younger son Jiming, laid a blade to the boy's throat, and said, "Surrender to us and your son will live."

sentences.zh: 杲卿不答。

translations.literal: Gaoqing did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing said nothing.

sentences.zh: 遂並盧逖殺之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they killed Jiming together with Lu Ti.
translations.idiomatic: They then killed Jiming and Lu Ti together.

sentences.zh: 杲卿至洛陽，祿山怒曰：「吾擢爾太守，何所負而反？」

translations.literal: When Gaoqing reached Luoyang, Lushan said in anger, "I promoted you to prefect—what did I fail to give you that you rebelled?"
translations.idiomatic: When Gaoqing was brought to Luoyang, Lushan raged: "I made you prefect—what debt did I owe you that you turned against me?"

sentences.zh: 杲卿瞋目罵曰：「汝營州牧羊羯奴耳，竊荷恩寵，天子負汝何事，而乃反乎？

translations.literal: Gaoqing glared and cursed: "You are but a Jie slave who herded sheep in Yingzhou, who stole the emperor's favor—what did the Son of Heaven fail to give you that you rebelled?
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing glared and shouted back: "You are nothing but a Jie shepherd from Yingzhou who stole the throne's favor. What did the Son of Heaven ever owe you that you dared rebel?

sentences.zh: 我世唐臣，守忠義，恨不斬汝以謝上，從從爾反耶？」

translations.literal: I am a Tang subject for generations, keeping loyalty and righteousness; I regret only that I could not behead you to answer to the sovereign—would I follow you in rebellion?"
translations.idiomatic: My family has served Tang for generations. I keep faith and duty, and only regret that I could not cut off your head to answer to my emperor. Do you think I would join your rebellion?"

sentences.zh: 祿山不勝忿，縛之天津橋柱，節解以肉啖之，詈不絕，賊鉤斷其舌，曰：「復能罵否？」

translations.literal: Lushan could not contain his rage, bound him to a pillar on the Tianjin Bridge, dismembered him joint by joint and fed him his own flesh, yet the curses did not cease; the rebels hooked out his tongue and said, "Can you still curse?"
translations.idiomatic: Lushan, beside himself, had him bound to a pillar on the Tianjin Bridge, cut him apart joint by joint, and fed him his own flesh, yet the curses never stopped. The rebels hooked out his tongue and sneered, "Can you still curse us now?"

sentences.zh: 杲卿含胡而絕，年六十五。

translations.literal: Gaoqing mumbled indistinctly and died, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing could only mumble through his ruined mouth and died, aged sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 履謙既斷手足，何千年弟適在傍，咀血噴其面，賊臠之，見者垂泣。

translations.literal: After Lüqian's hands and feet were cut off, He Qiannian's younger brother happened to be at his side; Lüqian chewed blood and spat it in his face, and the rebels carved him to pieces; those who saw it wept.
translations.idiomatic: After Lüqian's limbs were severed, He Qiannian's younger brother stood nearby. Lüqian chewed blood and spat it in the man's face, and the rebels hacked him apart. All who watched wept.

sentences.zh: 杲卿宗子近屬皆被害。

translations.literal: Gaoqing's clansmen and close kin were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Every clansman and close kinsman of Gaoqing's line was put to death.

sentences.zh: 杲卿已虜，諸郡復為賊守。

translations.literal: Once Gaoqing was captive, the commanderies again came under rebel control.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaoqing was taken, the commanderies fell back into rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 張通幽以兄相賊，譖杲卿於楊國忠，故不加贈。

translations.literal: Zhang Tongyou, because his elder brother had sided with the rebels, slandered Gaoqing to Yang Guozhong, and therefore no posthumous honors were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tongyou's elder brother had joined the rebels, so Tongyou slandered Gaoqing to Yang Guozhong, and for that reason no posthumous honors were granted at first.

sentences.zh: 肅宗在鳳翔，真卿表其枉，會通幽為普安太守，上皇杖殺之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong was at Fengxiang, Zhenqing memorialized that he had been wronged; it happened that Tongyou was prefect of Pu'an, and the retired emperor had him beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengxiang, Suzong received Zhenqing's memorial on the injustice. Tongyou was then prefect of Pu'an, and the retired emperor had him beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 李光弼、郭子儀收常山，出杲卿、履謙二家親屬數百人於獄，厚給遺，令行喪。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi and Guo Ziyi recovered Changshan, released several hundred kin of the two families of Gaoqing and Lüqian from prison, gave them generous support, and ordered mourning performed.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Guangbi and Guo Ziyi retook Changshan, they freed several hundred relatives of Gaoqing's and Lüqian's households from prison, gave them generous support, and saw that proper mourning was carried out.

sentences.zh: 乾元初，贈杲卿太子太保，謚曰忠節，封其妻崔清河郡夫人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianyuan era Gaoqing was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, given the posthumous title Loyal and Upright, and his wife Cui was enfeoffed as Lady of Qinghe Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianyuan era Gaoqing was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Loyal and Upright, and his wife Lady Cui was enfeoffed as Lady of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 初，博士裴郡以杲卿不執政，但謚曰忠，議者不平，故以二惠謚焉。

translations.literal: At first Academician Pei Jun, because Gaoqing had not held high office, gave only the posthumous title Loyal; critics were dissatisfied, and therefore the two-character title was used.
translations.idiomatic: At first Academician Pei Jun, noting that Gaoqing had never held high central office, proposed only the single character Loyal for his posthumous name. Critics objected, and the fuller title Loyal and Upright was adopted.

sentences.zh: 逖、季明及宗子等皆贈五品官。

translations.literal: Ti, Jiming, and the clansmen's sons were all posthumously given fifth-rank offices.
translations.idiomatic: Ti, Jiming, and the sons of the clan were all granted posthumous fifth-rank offices.

sentences.zh: 建中中，又贈杲卿司徒。

translations.literal: In the Jianzhong era Gaoqing was again posthumously made Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianzhong reign he was posthumously raised again to Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 初，杲卿被殺，徇首於衢，莫敢收。

translations.literal: When Gaoqing was first killed, his head was paraded in the streets and no one dared collect it.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaoqing was killed, his head was displayed in the streets, and no one dared claim it.

sentences.zh: 有張湊者，得其發，持謁上皇。

translations.literal: A man named Zhang Cou obtained his hair and went to present it to the retired emperor.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Zhang Cou recovered a lock of his hair and brought it before the retired emperor.

sentences.zh: 是昔見夢，帝寤，為祭。

translations.literal: That night he appeared in a dream; the emperor awoke and performed sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: That night Gaoqing appeared to him in a dream. The emperor woke and offered sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 後湊歸發於其妻，妻疑之，發若動雲。

translations.literal: Later Cou returned the hair to his wife; she was suspicious, for the hair seemed to move like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Later Cou brought the hair home to his wife. She was uneasy, for the strands seemed to stir like drifting clouds.

sentences.zh: 後泉明購屍將葬，得刑者言，死時一足先斷，與履謙同坎瘞。

translations.literal: Later Quanming purchased the corpse for burial; from the executioner he learned that at death one foot had already been severed, and that he was buried in the same pit as Lüqian.
translations.idiomatic: Later Quanming bought the body for burial. An executioner told him that one foot had already been cut off at death and that Gaoqing lay in the same grave as Lüqian.

sentences.zh: 指其域得之，乃葬長安鳳棲原。

translations.literal: He pointed out the place and recovered them, then buried them at Fengqi Plain in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Guided to the spot, he recovered the remains and buried them at Fengqi Plain in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 季明、逖同塋。

translations.literal: Jiming and Ti shared the same tomb mound.
translations.idiomatic: Jiming and Ti were laid in the same grave.

sentences.zh: 泉明有孝節，喜振人之急。

translations.literal: Quanming possessed filial devotion and integrity and delighted in relieving others in distress.
translations.idiomatic: Quanming was known for filial devotion and integrity and took pleasure in helping others in desperate need.

sentences.zh: 既為承業所遣，未至而常山陷，故客壽陽。

translations.literal: Having been sent back by Chengye, he had not yet arrived when Changshan fell, and so he lodged as a guest in Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye had sent him back before he could return, and Changshan fell while he was still on the road, so he stayed on as a guest in Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 史思明圍李光弼，獲泉明，裹以革，送幽州，間關得免。

translations.literal: Shi Siming besieged Li Guangbi, captured Quanming, wrapped him in leather, and sent him to Youzhou; he escaped after many perils.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming besieged Li Guangbi he captured Quanming, bound him in hides, and sent him toward Youzhou, but Quanming escaped after many close calls.

sentences.zh: 思明歸國，而真卿方為蒲州刺史，令泉明到河北求宗屬。

translations.literal: When Siming returned to allegiance, Zhenqing was then prefect of Pu and ordered Quanming to go to Hebei to seek out clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: After Siming submitted again to the court, Zhenqing was prefect of Pu and sent Quanming into Hebei to find their kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 始，一女及姑女並流離賊中，及是並得之，悉錢三萬贖姑女還，取貲復往，則己女復失之。

translations.literal: At first one daughter and a paternal aunt's daughter were both adrift among the rebels; now he found them both, spent all thirty thousand cash to ransom the aunt's daughter and send her back, took funds and went again, and then lost his own daughter once more.
translations.idiomatic: His own daughter and a cousin's daughter had both been lost to the rebels. He now found them, spent every coin he had—thirty thousand cash—to ransom the cousin's child and send her home, raised more funds and went back, and lost track of his own daughter again.

sentences.zh: 履謙及父故將妻子奴隸尚三百餘人，轉徙不自存，泉明悉力贍給，分多勻薄，相扶挾度河托真卿。

translations.literal: Lüqian's and his father's former officers' wives, children, and slaves still numbered more than three hundred, wandering without means to live; Quanming supported them with all his strength, dividing more or less evenly, helping one another across the river and entrusting them to Zhenqing.
translations.idiomatic: More than three hundred people—Lüqian's household, his father's old officers, their wives, children, and servants—were wandering destitute. Quanming supported them as best he could, sharing what he had fairly, and helped them cross the river to Zhenqing.

sentences.zh: 真卿隨所歸資送之。

translations.literal: Zhenqing, according to where each went, supplied funds and sent them off.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing gave each party funds according to where they were bound and sent them on their way.

sentences.zh: 泉明之殯父，與履謙分柩，護還長安。

translations.literal: Quanming buried his father, shared the coffin with Lüqian, and escorted the remains back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Quanming buried his father, shared the coffin with Lüqian's remains, and escorted them back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 履謙妻疑斂具儉狹，發視之，與杲卿等，乃號踴，待泉明如父。

translations.literal: Lüqian's wife suspected the burial goods were meager and narrow; she opened the coffin to look and found them equal to Gaoqing's; then she wailed and leaped in mourning and treated Quanming like a father.
translations.idiomatic: Lüqian's wife feared the burial had been stinted. When she opened the coffin she found her husband laid out with the same honor as Gaoqing. She broke into loud mourning and thereafter treated Quanming as she would a father.

sentences.zh: 肅宗拜泉明郫令，政化清明，誅宿盜，人情翕然。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong appointed Quanming magistrate of Pi; his governance was clear, he executed long-standing robbers, and popular sentiment drew together.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong appointed Quanming magistrate of Pi. His rule was clear and firm, he executed entrenched bandits, and the people rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 成都尹舉其課第一，遷彭州司馬。

translations.literal: The Chengdu intendant ranked his performance first and he was transferred to be military aide of Pengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The intendant of Chengdu rated his performance the best in the circuit, and he was promoted to military aide of Pengzhou.

sentences.zh: 家貧，居官廉，而孤藐相從百口，飦鬻不給，無慍嘆。

translations.literal: His family was poor; in office he was incorrupt, yet orphans and the weak following him numbered a hundred mouths, and gruel could not suffice—yet he showed no anger or complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Though his household was poor and he lived frugally in office, more than a hundred orphans and dependents followed him. Often there was not enough porridge to go around, yet he never showed anger or resentment.

sentences.zh: 居母喪，毀骨立。

translations.literal: In mourning for his mother he wasted away until only skin and bone remained.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his mother he grieved until he was skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 其行義，當世以為難。

translations.literal: His conduct and righteousness were regarded in his age as hard to match.
translations.idiomatic: Men of his day held his conduct and moral courage to be extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 春卿，倜儻美姿儀，通當世務。

translations.literal: Chunqing was free-spirited, handsome in bearing, and versed in affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Chunqing was bold and open in spirit, handsome in bearing, and thoroughly versed in the affairs of his day.

sentences.zh: 十六舉明經、拔萃高第，調犀浦主簿。

translations.literal: At sixteen he passed the Mingjing and Baodi examinations with high marks and was appointed chief clerk of Xipu.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he passed the Mingjing and Baodi examinations with top marks and was posted as chief clerk of Xipu.

sentences.zh: 嘗送徒於州，亡其籍，至廷，口記物色，凡千人，無所差。

translations.literal: Once when escorting convicts to the prefecture he lost the register; at court he recited from memory their features—nearly a thousand men—and made no error.
translations.idiomatic: Once, escorting convicts to the prefectural seat, he lost the register. At court he described every man from memory—nearly a thousand in all—and did not mistake a single one.

sentences.zh: 長史陸象先異之，轉蜀尉。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Lu Xiangxian was struck by him and transferred him to be sheriff of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Lu Xiangxian was so impressed that he moved him to a sheriff's post in Shu.

sentences.zh: 蘇颋代為長史，被譖系獄，為《棕櫚賦》自托，颋遽出之。

translations.literal: When Su Ting replaced him as chief administrator, Chunqing was slandered and imprisoned; he wrote the "Palm Rhapsody" to plead his case, and Ting at once released him.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Ting became chief administrator, Chunqing was slandered and thrown into prison. He wrote the "Palm Rhapsody" to plead his case, and Ting released him at once.

sentences.zh: 魏征遠孫瞻罪抵死，春卿為請玉真公主，得不死，時人高其節。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng's distant descendant Zhan was guilty of a capital crime; Chunqing pleaded with Princess Yuzhen and he was not put to death; men of the time honored his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng's distant descendant Zhan faced execution for a capital crime. Chunqing appealed to Princess Yuzhen and saved his life. Contemporaries admired his moral courage.

sentences.zh: 終偃師丞。

translations.literal: He ended his career as assistant magistrate of Yanshi.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his days as assistant magistrate of Yanshi.

sentences.zh: 臨終，捉真卿臂曰：「爾當大吾族，顧我不得見，以諸子諉汝。」

translations.literal: On his deathbed he seized Zhenqing's arm and said, "You will enlarge our clan; alas I shall not see it— I entrust my sons to you."
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he seized Zhenqing's arm and said, "You will bring greatness to our clan. I shall not live to see it, so I leave my sons in your care."

sentences.zh: 後真卿主其昏嫁。

translations.literal: Later Zhenqing arranged their marriages.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing later saw to their marriages.

sentences.zh: 沈盈者，亦杲卿甥，有行義，明黃老學。

translations.literal: Shen Ying was also Gaoqing's nephew by marriage; he had integrity and was versed in Huang-Lao learning.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Ying, another nephew of Gaoqing's, was a man of integrity and well versed in Huang-Lao thought.

sentences.zh: 解褐博野尉，與杲卿同死難，贈大理正，官其二子遙、達。」

translations.literal: Upon leaving the russet he became sheriff of Boye, died with Gaoqing in the same ordeal, was posthumously made Director of the Court of Judicial Review, and his two sons Yao and Da were given offices."
translations.idiomatic: He left private life to serve as sheriff of Boye, died with Gaoqing in the same ordeal, was posthumously made Director of the Court of Judicial Review, and offices were granted to his sons Yao and Da."

sentences.zh: 賈循者，京兆華原人，其先家常山。

translations.literal: Jia Xun was a native of Huayuan in Jingzhao; his forebears had long been in Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xun came from Huayuan in Jingzhao; his family had long been settled in Changshan.

sentences.zh: 父會，有高節嘗稱疾不答辟署，裏中號「一龍」。

translations.literal: His father Hui had lofty integrity and once pleaded illness and would not accept summons to office; the neighborhood called him "the lone dragon."
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui was a man of lofty integrity who once pleaded illness and refused every summons to office; neighbors called him "the lone dragon."

sentences.zh: 親亡，負土成墓，廬其左，手蒔松柏，時號「關中曾子」。

translations.literal: When his parents died he carried earth to make the tomb, built a mourning hut to the left, planted pine and cypress by hand, and was styled at the time "the Zengzi of Guanzhong."
translations.idiomatic: When his parents died he carried earth to build their tomb, raised a mourning hut beside it, and planted pine and cypress with his own hands. Men of the time called him "the Zengzi of Guanzhong."

sentences.zh: 卒，縣人私謚曰廣孝征君。

translations.literal: When he died the county people privately gave him the posthumous title Lord of Expansive Filiality, Recluse.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the people of the county privately styled him Lord of Expansive Filiality, Recluse.

sentences.zh: 循有大略，禮部尚書蘇颋嘗謂今頗、牧，及為益州，表署列將。

translations.literal: Xun had great strategic vision; Minister of Rites Su Ting once said he was a present-day Yan and Mu, and when Ting was in Yizhou he memorialized to appoint him among the commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Xun possessed great strategic vision. Su Ting, minister of rites, once said he was a Yan and Mu of the present age, and when Ting served in Yizhou he recommended him for command among the generals.

sentences.zh: 敗吐蕃於西山，三遷靜塞軍營田使。

translations.literal: He defeated the Tibetans at Western Mountain and was transferred three times to be agricultural colony commissioner of Jingsai Army.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the Tibetans in the western hills and was promoted three times, ending as agricultural colony commissioner of the Jingsai Army.

sentences.zh: 張守珪北伐，次灤河，屬凍泮，欲濟無梁。

translations.literal: When Zhang Shougui marched north he halted at the Luan River; the ice had thawed and he wished to cross but there was no bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On Zhang Shougui's northern campaign the army halted at the Luan River just as the ice broke up. They needed to cross but had no bridge.

sentences.zh: 循揣廣狹為橋以濟，破虜而還，以功擢遊擊將軍、榆關守捉使。

translations.literal: Xun gauged the breadth and built a bridge to cross, routed the barbarians and returned, and for his merit was promoted to irregular general and defender of Yuguan.
translations.idiomatic: Xun measured the channel, built a bridge to get the army across, routed the enemy, and returned. For this feat he was made irregular general and defender of Yuguan Pass.

sentences.zh: 地南負海，北屬長城，林埌岑翳，寇所蔽伏。

translations.literal: The land south bears upon the sea, north adjoins the Great Wall; forests and hills are dense and shaded—a place where bandits hide.
translations.idiomatic: The region bordered the sea to the south and the Great Wall to the north, its woods and hills thick with cover where raiders could lie in ambush.

sentences.zh: 循調土斬木開道，賊遁去。

translations.literal: Xun mobilized the local people, felled trees, and opened a road; the bandits fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Xun rallied the locals to cut timber and clear a road, and the bandits withdrew.

sentences.zh: 范陽節度使李適之薦為安東副大都護。

translations.literal: Fan-Yang military governor Li Shizhi recommended him as vice grand protector of Andong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shizhi, military governor of Fanyang, recommended him for appointment as deputy grand protector of the Eastern Pacification.

sentences.zh: 安祿山兼平盧節度，表為副，遷博陵太守。

translations.literal: An Lushan also held Pinglu command; he memorialized [Xun] as his deputy and had him transferred to be prefect of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan also took command of Pinglu, he petitioned to have Xun serve as his deputy and had him appointed prefect of Boling.

sentences.zh: 祿山欲擊奚、契丹，復奏循光祿卿自副，使知留後。

translations.literal: Lushan wished to attack the Xi and Khitan; he again memorialized that Xun be made Guanglu Qing as his own deputy, and had him act as regent in his absence.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan planned to campaign against the Xi and Khitan, he again petitioned for Xun to be made Minister of Imperial Entertainments and serve as his deputy, leaving him in charge as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 九姓叛，祿山兼節度河東，而循亦兼雁門副之。

translations.literal: When the Nine Surnames rebelled, Lushan also took command of Hedong, and Xun concurrently served as deputy at Yanmen as well.
translations.idiomatic: After the Nine Surnames rose in revolt, Lushan added Hedong to his commands, and Xun was concurrently appointed deputy governor at Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 母亡將葬，宅有枯桑，一夕再生，芝出北庸，人以為瑞。

translations.literal: When his mother died and was about to be buried, there was a withered mulberry tree at the house; in one night it sprouted anew, and a lingzhi mushroom appeared in the north courtyard—people took this as an auspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: As his mother lay dead awaiting burial, a dead mulberry tree in the family compound put forth fresh growth overnight, and a lingzhi fungus appeared in the north courtyard; people regarded it as a good omen.

sentences.zh: 玄宗以循有功，詔贈其父常山太守。

translations.literal: Because Xun had rendered service, Emperor Xuanzong issued an edict posthumously granting his father the title of prefect of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of Xun's achievements, Emperor Xuanzong issued an edict posthumously ennobling his father as prefect of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 祿山反，使循守幽州，故杲卿招之，以傾賊巢穴，循許可。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, he sent Xun to hold Youzhou; the former Yan Gaoqing recruited him to overturn the rebels' nest, and Xun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, he posted Xun to defend Youzhou. Yan Gaoqing, who had formerly served there, summoned him to strike at the rebel stronghold, and Xun consented.

sentences.zh: 為向潤客等發其謀，賊縊之。

translations.literal: Xiang Runke and others exposed his plot, and the rebels strangled him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Runke and others betrayed the conspiracy, and the rebels hanged him.

sentences.zh: 建中二年，贈太尉，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong, [the court] posthumously granted him the title of Grand Preceptor and gave him the posthumous name Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: In 781, he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous name Zhong, "Loyal."

sentences.zh: 從子隱林，為永平兵馬使。

translations.literal: His nephew Yin Lin served as military commissioner of Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Yin Lin held the post of military commissioner at Yongping.

sentences.zh: 當入衛，屬朱泚難，率眾扈行在。

translations.literal: When he was about to enter the capital on guard duty, Zhu Ci's rebellion broke out, and he led his troops to escort the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: He was on his way to the capital to take up palace guard duty when Zhu Ci's revolt erupted, and he led his men to protect the emperor's mobile court.

sentences.zh: 德宗見隱林，偉其貌，問家世，答曰：「故范陽節度副使循，臣從父也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong saw Yin Lin, admired his imposing appearance, and asked about his family. He answered: "The former Fan-Yang deputy military commissioner Xun was my father's cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong was struck by Yin Lin's imposing bearing and asked about his lineage. Yin Lin replied, "My father's cousin was Jia Xun, former deputy military governor of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 帝異之，引至臥內，以手板畫地陳攻守計，即奏曰：「臣嘗夢日墜，以首承之。」

translations.literal: The emperor was astonished, led him into the inner chamber, and, using his hand tablet to trace plans on the ground, set forth strategies of attack and defense; then he reported: "I once dreamed that the sun fell, and I caught it on my head."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was intrigued and brought him into his private quarters. Yin Lin traced battle plans on the floor with his official tablet, then said, "I once dreamed the sun fell from the sky and I caught it on my head."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「非朕邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Was that not I?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Was that not me?"

sentences.zh: 因令糾察行在，遷檢校右散騎常侍，封武威郡王。

translations.literal: He therefore had him inspect the traveling court, promoted him to acting Right Regular Attendant, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Wuwei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On that basis he was put in charge of policing the traveling court, promoted to acting Right Regular Attendant, and enfeoffed as Prince of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 賊圍急，隱林與侯仲莊冒矢石死戰。

translations.literal: When the rebel siege grew desperate, Yin Lin and Hou Zhongzhuang braved arrows and stones and fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebel siege tightened, Yin Lin and Hou Zhongzhuang fought through a hail of arrows and stones as if death meant nothing.

sentences.zh: 已而解，從臣稱慶，隱林流涕前曰：「泚已奔，群臣大慶宗社無疆之休，然陛下資性急，不能容掩。

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted, the attendant ministers offered congratulations; Yin Lin came forward in tears and said, "Ci has already fled. The ministers rejoice greatly that the altars of state may know boundless peace, yet Your Majesty's temperament is quick and cannot brook concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Once the siege was broken, the courtiers broke into celebration. Yin Lin stepped forward in tears and said, "Zhu Ci has fled, and we all rejoice that the dynasty may endure. Yet Your Majesty is quick-tempered and cannot abide the least concealment.

sentences.zh: 若不悛，雖今賊亡，憂未艾也。」

translations.literal: If you do not mend your ways, though the rebels are gone today, your troubles will not yet be ended.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not change, the rebels may be gone now, but your troubles will not end with them.

sentences.zh: 帝不以為忤，拜神策統軍。

translations.literal: The emperor did not take offense and appointed him commander of the Shence Army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took no offense and appointed him commander of the Shence Army.

sentences.zh: 卒，帝思其質直，贈尚書左仆射，以實戶三百封其家。

translations.literal: When he died, the emperor remembered his plain forthrightness, posthumously granted him Left Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs, and enfeoffed his household with three hundred tax households.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, the emperor recalled his blunt honesty, posthumously made him Left Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs, and granted his family an estate of three hundred tax households.

sentences.zh: 張巡字巡，鄧州南陽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Xun, courtesy name Xun, was a man of Nanyang in Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun, styled Xun, was a native of Nanyang in Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 博通群書，曉戰陣法。

translations.literal: He broadly mastered the classics and understood methods of battle formation.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply read in the classics and well versed in the art of war.

sentences.zh: 氣誌高邁，略細節，所交必大人長者，不與庸俗合，時人叵知也。

translations.literal: His spirit was lofty and far-reaching; he overlooked small details. Those he befriended were always eminent elders; he would not associate with vulgar men—people of the time could not understand him.
translations.idiomatic: High-minded and broad in spirit, he cared little for petty detail. He sought out only men of stature and integrity, shunning the commonplace, and his contemporaries found him hard to fathom.

sentences.zh: 開元末，擢進士第。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaiyuan era he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Near the close of the Kaiyuan reign he earned his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 時兄曉已位監察御史，皆以名稱重一時。

translations.literal: At that time his elder brother Xiao already held the post of investigating censor; both were famed and esteemed throughout the age.
translations.idiomatic: By then his elder brother Zhang Xiao was already an investigating censor, and both brothers enjoyed great renown.

sentences.zh: 巡由太子通事舍人出為清河令，治績最，而負節義，或以困厄歸者，傾貲振護無吝。

translations.literal: Xun went out from his post as attendant to the crown prince to become magistrate of Qinghe; his administrative record was the finest, and he possessed integrity and righteousness—when any in hardship returned, he poured out his wealth to aid and protect them without stint.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving his post as attendant to the crown prince, Zhang Xun became magistrate of Qinghe, where his governance ranked first in the realm. A man of honor, he gave freely of his fortune to shelter and support those who came to him in distress.

sentences.zh: 秩滿還都。

translations.literal: When his term expired he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 於是楊國忠方專國，權勢可炙。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Guozhong was monopolizing the state; his power and influence were scorching hot.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong then dominated the court, his power so fierce it seemed to burn the hand that touched it.

sentences.zh: 或勸一見，且顯用，答曰：「是方為國怪祥，朝宦不可為也。」

translations.literal: Some urged him to pay one visit and thereby win prominent appointment. He answered, "That man is becoming the state's ominous portent—office at court is not to be sought.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to pay Yang a visit and win high office. He replied, "That man is a calamity upon the state. I want no part of court rank under him.

sentences.zh: 更調真源令。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to be magistrate of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned instead as magistrate of Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 土多豪猾，大吏華南金樹威恣肆，邑中語曰：「南金口，明府手。」

translations.literal: The district had many fierce and cunning men; the senior clerk Hua Nanjin built up his power and acted without restraint. A saying in the county ran: "Nanjin's mouth, the magistrate's hand.
translations.idiomatic: The district swarmed with bold ruffians, and the chief clerk Hua Nanjin had grown tyrannical. Local people said, "Whatever Nanjin asks for, the magistrate grants.

sentences.zh: 巡下車，以法誅之，赦餘黨，莫不改行遷善。

translations.literal: When Xun took office he executed him by law, pardoned the remaining followers, and none failed to reform and turn to good.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Xun took office he had Hua Nanjin executed according to law, pardoned the rest of his gang, and not one failed to mend his ways.

sentences.zh: 政簡約，民甚宜之。

translations.literal: His government was simple and restrained, and the people found it very agreeable.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was spare and fair, and the people flourished under it.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，天寶十五載正月，賊酋張通晤陷宋、曹等州，譙郡太守楊萬石降賊，逼巡為長史，使西迎賊軍。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, in the first month of the fifteenth year of Tianbao the rebel chieftain Zhang Tongwu captured Song, Cao, and other prefectures; Qiao Prefecture governor Yang Wanshi surrendered to the rebels, forced Xun to serve as chief administrator, and sent him west to welcome the rebel army.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose in rebellion, in the first month of 755 the rebel leader Zhang Tongwu seized Songzhou, Caozhou, and neighboring prefectures. Yang Wanshi, governor of Qiao Prefecture, surrendered and compelled Zhang Xun to serve as his chief aide, then ordered him west to greet the rebel forces.

sentences.zh: 巡率吏哭玄元皇帝祠，遂起兵討賊，從者千餘。

translations.literal: Xun led the officials in weeping at the shrine of the Mysterious Origin Emperor, then raised troops to suppress the rebels; more than a thousand followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun led his officials in mourning at the shrine of the Mysterious Origin Emperor, then took up arms against the rebels. More than a thousand men rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 初，靈昌太守嗣吳王祗受詔合河南兵拒祿山，有單父尉賈賁者，閬州刺史璿之子，率吏稱吳王兵，擊宋州。

translations.literal: Earlier, Lingchang Prefecture governor Heir Prince of Wu Wang Zhi had received an edict to gather Henan troops to resist Lushan. There was a Danyang district captain named Jia Ben, son of Langzhou Prefect Xuan, who led officials in the name of the Prince of Wu's army and attacked Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wang Zhi, Prince of Wu and governor of Lingchang, had received orders to assemble Henan forces against An Lushan. A district captain of Danyang named Jia Ben—son of Langzhou prefect Xuan—raised troops in the prince's name and attacked Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 通晤走襄邑，為頓丘令盧韺所殺。

translations.literal: Tongwu fled to Xiangyi and was killed by Dunqiu magistrate Lu Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tongwu fled to Xiangyi, where he was killed by Lu Yin, magistrate of Dunqiu.

sentences.zh: 賁引軍進至雍丘，巡與之合，有眾二千。

translations.literal: Ben led his army forward to Yongqiu; Xun joined with him, and together they had two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Ben marched on Yongqiu, where Zhang Xun joined him; together they fielded two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 是時雍丘令令狐潮舉縣附賊，遂自將東敗淮陽兵，虜其眾，反接在廷，將殺之，暫出行部。

translations.literal: At that time Yongqiu magistrate Linghu Chao had raised the whole county to join the rebels; he then personally led troops east, defeated the Huaiyang force, captured their men, bound them hand and foot in the hall, and was about to execute them when he temporarily went out on an inspection tour.
translations.idiomatic: By then Linghu Chao, magistrate of Yongqiu, had surrendered the entire county to the rebels. He marched east, routed the Huaiyang garrison, took the survivors prisoner, bound them in the hall pending execution, and then left briefly on official business.

sentences.zh: 淮陽囚更解縛，起殺守者，迎賁等入。

translations.literal: The Huaiyang prisoners again untied their bonds, rose up and killed the guards, and welcomed Ben and the others inside.
translations.idiomatic: The Huaiyang captives broke free, killed their guards, and opened the gates to Jia Ben and his men.

sentences.zh: 潮不得歸，巡乃屠其妻子，礫城上。

translations.literal: Chao could not return; Xun then slaughtered his wife and children and piled [their bodies] on the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to return, Linghu Chao looked on as Zhang Xun had his wife and children put to death and their bodies displayed on the battlements.

sentences.zh: 祗聞，承制拜賁監察御史。

translations.literal: When Zhi heard of this, by imperial order he appointed Ben investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing of this, Wang Zhi, acting on imperial authority, appointed Jia Ben investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 潮怨賁，還攻雍丘，賁趨門，為眾躪死。

translations.literal: Chao resented Ben, returned to attack Yongqiu; Ben rushed to the gate and was trampled to death by the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Chao, nursing a grudge against Jia Ben, returned to assault Yongqiu. Ben ran to the gate and was trampled to death in the press of battle.

sentences.zh: 巡馳騎決戰，身被創不顧，士乃奉巡主軍。

translations.literal: Xun galloped forth for a decisive battle; though wounded he paid no heed, and the soldiers thereupon upheld Xun as commander of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun charged out for a decisive fight. Though wounded, he never faltered, and the troops thereupon accepted him as their commander.

sentences.zh: 間道表諸朝，騰箋祗府，祗乃舉兗以東委巡經略。

translations.literal: By secret route he memorialized the court and sent urgent dispatches to Zhi's headquarters; Zhi then entrusted everything east of Yan to Xun's military management.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun sent secret reports to the court and urgent messages to Wang Zhi's headquarters. Wang Zhi then entrusted all territory east of Yanzhou to his command.

sentences.zh: 潮以賊眾四萬薄城，人大恐。

translations.literal: Chao came with forty thousand rebel troops to press the city, and the people were greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Chao advanced on the city with forty thousand rebel troops, and the populace was seized with terror.

sentences.zh: 巡諭諸將曰：「賊知城中虛實，有輕我心。

translations.literal: Xun instructed the generals, saying, "The rebels know the city's true strength and look down on us.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun told his officers, "The enemy knows how weak we really are and despises us for it.

sentences.zh: 今出不意，可驚而潰也，乘之，勢必折。」

translations.literal: If we now strike where they do not expect it, we can startle them into rout; press the advantage, and they are sure to break.
translations.idiomatic: Strike where they do not expect us, and we can shock them into flight. Press hard, and they will surely collapse.

sentences.zh: 諸將曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The generals said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The officers agreed: "Well said."

sentences.zh: 巡乃分千人乘城，以數隊出，身前驅，直薄潮軍，軍卻。

translations.literal: Xun then divided a thousand men to man the walls, sent out several squads, himself leading the van, and drove straight at Chao's army; the army fell back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun left a thousand men on the walls and led several squads out himself at the head of the charge, driving straight into Linghu Chao's lines until the enemy fell back.

sentences.zh: 明日賊攻城，設百樓，巡柵城上，束芻灌膏以焚焉，賊不敢向，巡伺隙擊之。

translations.literal: The next day the rebels assaulted the city and erected a hundred siege towers; Xun built palisades on the wall, bound straw, soaked it in oil, and burned them, and the rebels did not dare approach; Xun watched for openings and struck them.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the rebels attacked with a hundred siege towers. Zhang Xun raised barricades along the wall, soaked bundles of straw in oil, and set the towers ablaze. The enemy dared not come near, and he harried them whenever he saw an opening.

sentences.zh: 積六旬，大小數百戰，士帶甲食，裹瘡鬥，潮遂敗走，追之，幾獲。

translations.literal: Over sixty days they fought several hundred engagements, large and small; the soldiers ate in armor and fought with bound wounds, until Chao was defeated and fled; they pursued him and nearly captured him.
translations.idiomatic: For sixty days they fought hundreds of battles, large and small. The men ate in their armor and fought with fresh bandages still on their wounds. At last Linghu Chao broke and fled; they pursued him nearly to capture.

sentences.zh: 潮怒，復率眾來。

translations.literal: Chao was enraged and again led his troops back.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Linghu Chao gathered his forces and returned.

sentences.zh: 然素善巡，至城下，情語巡曰：「本朝危蹙，兵不能出關，天下事去矣。

translations.literal: Yet he had always been on good terms with Xun; arriving below the wall, he spoke to Xun from the heart, saying, "The dynasty is in peril; its armies cannot break out of the passes—the affairs of the realm are lost.
translations.idiomatic: He had always been on friendly terms with Zhang Xun, and now, coming to the foot of the wall, he spoke to him frankly: "The dynasty is dying. Imperial armies cannot break out of the passes. The empire is already lost.

sentences.zh: 足下以羸兵守危堞，忠無所立，盍相從以茍富貴乎？」

translations.literal: You hold these perilous walls with exhausted troops; there is nowhere for loyalty to stand. Why not join me and scrape together some wealth and rank?
translations.idiomatic: You are holding a doomed city with a handful of worn-out men. There is no glory in this loyalty. Come over to my side and at least save yourself some fortune and honor.

sentences.zh: 巡曰：「古者父死於君，義不報。

translations.literal: Xun said, "In antiquity, when a father died for his lord, a son did not seek revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun replied, "In ancient times, when a man died serving his lord, his son did not avenge the deed.

sentences.zh: 子乃銜妻孥怨，假力於賊以相圖，吾見君頭幹通衢，為百世笑，奈何？」

translations.literal: You now harbor resentment for wife and children, borrow the rebels' strength to plot against me—I see your head drying in the public thoroughfare, laughed at for a hundred generations. How can you do this?"
translations.idiomatic: You resent me for your wife and children, and now you would use the rebels' power to destroy me. I see your head rotting in the public square, a mockery for a hundred generations. Have you no shame?"

sentences.zh: 潮赧然去。

translations.literal: Chao, abashed, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Chao withdrew, flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 當此時，王命不復通，大將六人白巡以勢不敵，且上存亡莫知，不如降。

translations.literal: At this time imperial orders no longer reached them; six senior generals told Xun privately that the odds were impossible and that, with the emperor's fate unknown, it would be better to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: By then no orders came from the court. Six senior generals privately urged Zhang Xun that resistance was hopeless and that, with the emperor's fate unknown, surrender was the wiser course.

sentences.zh: 六人者，皆官開府、特進。

translations.literal: These six men all held the ranks of honorary grand general or special eminence.
translations.idiomatic: All six held exalted honorary ranks—opening grand general or special eminence.

sentences.zh: 巡陽許諾，明日堂上設天子畫像，率軍士朝，人人盡泣。

translations.literal: Xun feigned agreement; the next day he set up the emperor's portrait in the hall, led the soldiers in audience, and every man wept to exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun pretended to agree. The next day he placed the emperor's portrait in the hall and led the troops in homage until every man was weeping.

sentences.zh: 巡引六將至，責以大誼，斬之。

translations.literal: Xun then brought the six generals forward, rebuked them for violating the great principle, and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Then he summoned the six generals, denounced them for betraying their duty, and had them beheaded.

sentences.zh: 士心益勸。

translations.literal: The soldiers' hearts were all the more encouraged.
translations.idiomatic: The troops' resolve only grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 會糧乏，潮餉賊鹽米數百艘且至，巡夜壁城南，潮悉軍來拒，巡遣勇士銜枚濱河，取鹽米千斛，焚其餘而還。

translations.literal: When provisions ran short, Chao was supplying the rebels with several hundred boatloads of salt and grain that were about to arrive; Xun by night fortified the south of the city, Chao brought out his whole army to resist, and Xun sent brave men with gags in their mouths along the riverbank, took a thousand bushels of salt and grain, burned the rest, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: As food grew scarce, several hundred boatloads of salt and grain bound for the rebel camp were nearing the city. Zhang Xun strengthened the southern defenses by night. Linghu Chao marched out his entire force to block him, but Zhang Xun sent silent raiders along the riverbank to seize a thousand bushels of supplies, burn the rest, and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 城中矢盡，巡縛槁為人千餘，被黑衣，夜縋城下，潮兵爭射之，久，乃槁人；

translations.literal: When arrows in the city were exhausted, Xun bound straw into more than a thousand dummy figures, clothed them in black, and by night lowered them down the wall; Chao's soldiers vied to shoot them, and after a long while [they saw] they were straw men.
translations.idiomatic: When the city ran out of arrows, Zhang Xun fashioned more than a thousand scarecrows, dressed them in black, and lowered them from the walls by night. Linghu Chao's men shot at them furiously until, after a long while, they realized they were only straw.

sentences.zh: 還，得箭數十萬。

translations.literal: When [the figures] were retrieved, they obtained several hundred thousand arrows.
translations.idiomatic: When the dummies were hauled back up, the defenders recovered several hundred thousand arrows.

sentences.zh: 其後復夜縋人，賊笑，不設備，乃以死士五百斫潮營，軍大亂，焚壘幕，追奔十餘里。

translations.literal: Afterward they again lowered figures by night; the rebels laughed and made no preparations, whereupon five hundred death-defying soldiers stormed Chao's camp; the army fell into great disorder, [they] burned the tents and palisades, and pursued the fleeing enemy more than ten li.
translations.idiomatic: Later they lowered dummies again by night. The rebels laughed and took no precautions—whereupon five hundred picked warriors fell upon Linghu Chao's camp. The enemy lines broke in chaos; the raiders burned tents and stockades and chased the fugitives more than ten li.

sentences.zh: 賊慚，益兵圍之。

translations.literal: The rebels were shamed and increased their troops to besiege the city.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated, the rebels brought up reinforcements and tightened the siege.

sentences.zh: 薪水竭，巡紿潮：「欲引眾走，請退軍二舍，使我逸。」

translations.literal: When firewood and water were exhausted, Xun deceived Chao, saying, "I wish to lead the masses and flee; withdraw your army two stages and let us escape.
translations.idiomatic: When firewood and water ran out, Zhang Xun tricked Linghu Chao, saying, "I mean to break out with my men. Pull your army back two stages and give us room to escape.

sentences.zh: 潮不知其謀，許之。

translations.literal: Chao did not know his stratagem and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Chao, unaware of the ruse, agreed.

sentences.zh: 遂空城四出三十里，撤屋發木而還為備。

translations.literal: They then emptied the city and went out thirty li in all directions, tore down houses and pulled up timber, then returned to prepare defenses.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders then emptied the city and ranged thirty li in every direction, tearing down houses and stripping timber before returning to strengthen their defenses.

sentences.zh: 潮怒，圍復合。

translations.literal: Chao was enraged and closed in the siege again.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Linghu Chao closed the ring of siege once more.

sentences.zh: 巡徐謂潮曰：「君須此城，歸馬三十匹，我得馬且出奔，請君取城以藉口。」

translations.literal: Xun slowly said to Chao, "You need this city—return thirty horses, and once I have horses I will flee; please take the city as your excuse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun then told Linghu Chao calmly, "You want this city. Send back thirty horses, and once I have mounts I will break out—then you can take the city and save face.

sentences.zh: 潮歸馬，巡悉以給驍將，約曰：「賊至，人取一將。」

translations.literal: Chao returned the horses; Xun gave them all to his fiercest generals and agreed, saying, "When the rebels come, each man takes one general."
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Chao sent the horses back. Zhang Xun handed them all to his boldest officers with this order: "When the enemy comes, each of you seize one of their generals."

sentences.zh: 明日，潮責巡，答曰：「吾欲去，將士不從，奈何？」

translations.literal: The next day Chao reproached Xun; he answered, "I wished to leave, but the officers and soldiers would not follow—what could I do?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day Linghu Chao reproached him. Zhang Xun replied, "I wanted to go, but my officers and men refused to follow. What could I do?"

sentences.zh: 潮怒欲戰，陣未成，三十騎突出，禽將十四，斬百餘級，收器械牛馬。

translations.literal: Chao angrily wished to fight; before his formation was complete, thirty horsemen burst forth, captured fourteen generals, cut down more than a hundred men, and seized weapons, cattle, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Chao, furious, prepared to give battle—but before his lines were set, thirty horsemen burst out, seized fourteen enemy officers, killed more than a hundred men, and captured arms, cattle, and horses.

sentences.zh: 潮遁還陳留，不復出。

translations.literal: Chao fled back to Chenliu and did not come out again.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Chao fled back to Chenliu and never came out again.

sentences.zh: 七月，潮率賊將瞿伯玉攻城，遣偽使者四人傳賊命詔巡，巡斬以徇，余縶送祗所。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Chao led the rebel general Qu Boyu to attack the city and sent four false envoys bearing rebel edicts to summon Xun; Xun executed them as a public warning and bound the rest and sent them to Zhi's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Linghu Chao returned with the rebel general Qu Boyu to assault the city and sent four false envoys bearing rebel orders to Zhang Xun. He had them beheaded as a warning, bound the rest, and sent them to Wang Zhi.

sentences.zh: 圍凡四月，賊常數萬，而巡眾才千餘，每戰輒克。

translations.literal: The siege lasted four months in all; the rebels often numbered in the tens of thousands, while Xun's force was only a little over a thousand, yet in every battle they prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: The siege lasted four months altogether. The rebels often numbered in the tens of thousands, while Zhang Xun had barely a thousand men—yet he won every fight.

sentences.zh: 於是河南節度使嗣虢王巨屯彭城，假巡先鋒。

translations.literal: At this time Henan military governor Heir Prince of Guo Wang Ju was stationed at Pengcheng and made Xun his vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wang Ju, Prince of Guo and military governor of Henan, was encamped at Pengcheng and appointed Zhang Xun his vanguard.

sentences.zh: 俄而魯、東平陷賊，濟陰太守高承義舉郡叛，巨引兵東走臨淮。

translations.literal: Before long Lu and Dongping fell to the rebels; Jiyin Prefecture governor Gao Chengyi raised his whole command in rebellion, and Ju led his troops east and withdrew to Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lu and Dongping fell to the rebels. Gao Chengyi, governor of Jiyin, surrendered his entire command, and Wang Ju marched east, falling back to Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 賊將楊朝宗謀趨寧陵，絕巡餉路。

translations.literal: The rebel general Yang Chaozong planned to hurry to Ningling and cut off Xun's supply route.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Yang Chaozong planned to seize Ningling and sever Zhang Xun's supply lines.

sentences.zh: 巡外失巨依，拔眾保寧陵，馬裁三百，兵三千。

translations.literal: Xun, having lost Ju's support from outside, pulled up his forces and held Ningling; he had barely three hundred horses and three thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off from Wang Ju's support, Zhang Xun withdrew to Ningling with only three hundred horses and three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 至睢陽，與太守許遠、城父令姚訚等合。

translations.literal: He reached Suiyang and joined with Prefect Xu Yuan, Chengfù magistrate Yao Yin, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Suiyang and joined forces with the prefect Xu Yuan, the magistrate of Chengfu Yao Yin, and others.

sentences.zh: 乃遣將雷萬春、南霽雲等領兵戰寧陵北，斬賊將二十，殺萬餘人，投屍於汴，水為不流。

translations.literal: He then sent generals Lei Wanchun, Nan Jiyun, and others to lead troops in battle north of Ningling, beheading twenty rebel generals, killing more than ten thousand men, and casting corpses into the Bian River until the water would not flow.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Lei Wanchun, Nan Jiyun, and other officers to fight north of Ningling, where they beheaded twenty rebel commanders, killed more than ten thousand men, and threw the dead into the Bian River until its waters dammed and ceased to flow.

sentences.zh: 朝宗夜去。

translations.literal: Chaozong departed by night.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chaozong withdrew under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 有詔拜巡主客郎中，副河南節度使。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Xun chief minister of the host and deputy Henan military governor.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict appointed Zhang Xun chief minister of the host and deputy military governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 巡籍將士有功者請於巨，巨才授折沖、果毅。

translations.literal: Xun registered the officers and soldiers who had merit and requested rewards from Ju; Ju granted only the ranks of assault-resolute and brave-fruits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun submitted a roll of meritorious officers and men and asked Wang Ju to reward them. Wang Ju granted only the lower ranks of assault-resolute and brave-fruits.

sentences.zh: 巡諫曰：「宗社尚危，圍陵孤外，渠可吝賞與貲？」

translations.literal: Xun remonstrated, saying, "The altars of state are still in peril, and Ningling stands isolated outside the lines—how can you be stingy with honors and goods?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun protested: "The dynasty is still in mortal danger, and Ningling stands alone beyond the lines. How can you be miserly with honors and pay?

sentences.zh: 巨不聽。

translations.literal: Ju would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ju refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 至德二載，祿山死，慶緒遣其下尹子琦將同羅、突厥、奚勁兵與朝宗合，凡十餘萬，攻睢陽。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide, Lushan died; Qingxu sent his subordinate Yin Ziqi to lead fierce troops of Tongluo, Turks, and Xi together with Chaozong—more than a hundred thousand in all—to attack Suiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In 757, after An Lushan's death, his son An Qingxu sent Yin Ziqi at the head of Tongluo, Turk, and Xi crack troops to join Yang Chaozong—more than a hundred thousand men in all—in an assault on Suiyang.

sentences.zh: 巡勵士固守，日中二十戰，氣不衰。

translations.literal: Xun encouraged the soldiers to hold firm; they fought twenty battles by midday, and their spirit did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun roused his men to stand fast. By midday they had fought twenty engagements, and their fighting spirit never flagged.

sentences.zh: 遠自以材不及巡，請稟軍事而居其下，巡受不辭，遠專治軍糧戰具。

translations.literal: Yuan, considering his talent inferior to Xun's, asked to receive military orders while placing himself beneath him; Xun accepted without declining, and Yuan devoted himself solely to army provisions and war equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Judging his own abilities inferior to Zhang Xun's, Xu Yuan asked to take orders from him and serve under his command. Zhang Xun accepted without demur, and Xu Yuan devoted himself entirely to supplies and materiel.

sentences.zh: 前此，遠將李滔救東平，遂叛入賊，大將田秀榮潛與通。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yuan's officer Li Tao had gone to relieve Dongping, then defected to the rebels; the great general Tian Xiurong secretly communicated with the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xu Yuan's officer Li Tao had marched to relieve Dongping, then gone over to the rebels; the senior general Tian Xiurong was secretly in contact with the enemy.

sentences.zh: 或以告遠曰：「晨出戰，以碧帽為識。」

translations.literal: Someone reported to Yuan, saying, "Go out to battle at dawn and use blue caps as identification.
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned Xu Yuan, "If you sortie at dawn, mark your men with blue caps.

sentences.zh: 視之如言，盡覆其眾。

translations.literal: He looked and it was as said; he completely destroyed that force.
translations.idiomatic: He looked and found it exactly as foretold, and annihilated the entire force.

sentences.zh: 還輒曰：「我誘之也。」

translations.literal: On returning he always said, "I lured them.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he returned he would say, "I baited them.

sentences.zh: 請以精騎往，易錦帽。

translations.literal: He requested to go with elite cavalry and exchange [their] caps for brocade ones.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to ride out with picked cavalry and swap their caps for brocade ones.

sentences.zh: 遠以告巡，巡召登城，讓之，斬首示賊。

translations.literal: Yuan reported this to Xun; Xun had him summoned onto the wall, rebuked him, and beheaded him, displaying the head to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuan reported the matter to Zhang Xun. Zhang Xun had Li Tao called up onto the wall, rebuked him, and beheaded him, then displayed the head to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 因出薄戰，子琦敗，獲車馬牛羊，悉分士，秋豪無入其家。

translations.literal: Thereupon they sortied for close combat; Ziqi was defeated. Chariots, horses, cattle, and sheep were captured and all distributed among the soldiers—not the slightest portion entered his own household.
translations.idiomatic: They then sortied for a sharp engagement. Yin Ziqi was beaten. The chariots, horses, cattle, and sheep they captured were all divided among the men—not a hair's worth went into Zhang Xun's own stores.

sentences.zh: 有詔拜巡御史中丞，遠侍御史，訚吏部郎中。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Xun Censor-in-Chief, Yuan Attending Censor, and Yan Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict appointed Zhang Xun Censor-in-Chief, Xu Yuan Attending Censor, and Yao Yin a bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 巡欲乘勝擊陳留，子琦聞，復圍城。

translations.literal: Xun wished to press the victory and strike Chenliu; when Ziqi heard of it, he again besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun wanted to follow up the victory with an attack on Chenliu. When Yin Ziqi learned of it, he laid siege to the city again.

sentences.zh: 巡語其下曰：「吾蒙上恩，賊若復來，正有死耳。

translations.literal: Xun said to his subordinates, "I have received the emperor's grace. If the rebels come again, there is nothing before me but death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun told his officers, "The throne has shown me great favor. If the rebels return, death is all that awaits us.

sentences.zh: 諸君雖捐軀，而賞不直勛，以此痛恨！」

translations.literal: Though you gentlemen may give up your lives, the rewards will not match your merit—this fills me with bitter grief!
translations.idiomatic: You may lay down your lives, yet the honors paid will not equal your deeds. That is what grieves me most!

sentences.zh: 聞者感概。

translations.literal: Those who heard were deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard him were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 乃椎牛大饗，悉軍戰。

translations.literal: He then slaughtered oxen for a great feast and sent the whole army into battle.
translations.idiomatic: He slaughtered oxen for a great feast, then sent the entire army into battle.

sentences.zh: 賊望兵少，大笑。

translations.literal: The rebels saw how few his troops were and laughed aloud.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how few defenders there were, the rebels burst out laughing.

sentences.zh: 巡、遠親鼓之，賊潰，追北數十里。

translations.literal: Xun and Yuan personally beat the drums for them; the rebels broke and fled, and they pursued the routed enemy northward for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan beat the drums in person. The enemy broke and fled, and they chased the rout north for dozens of li.

sentences.zh: 其五月，賊刈麥，乃濟師。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the rebels reaped wheat, then brought their army across.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the rebels harvested the wheat, then moved their army across the river.

sentences.zh: 巡夜鳴鼓嚴隊，若將出。

translations.literal: At night Xun beat drums and drew up the ranks as if about to sortie.
translations.idiomatic: That night Zhang Xun beat the drums and formed the ranks as though he were about to break out.

sentences.zh: 賊申警。

translations.literal: The rebels doubled their guard.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels tightened their watch all through the night.

sentences.zh: 俄自鼓，賊覘城上兵休，乃弛備。

translations.literal: Soon he stopped drumming himself; the rebels spied and saw the troops on the wall resting, and so relaxed their defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he ceased drumming. The rebels spied the walls and saw the defenders at rest, and let their guard down.

sentences.zh: 巡使南霽雲等開門徑抵子琦所，斬將拔旗。

translations.literal: Xun sent Nan Jiyun and others to open the gates and go straight to where Ziqi was, beheading officers and tearing down flags.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun sent Nan Jiyun and others to fling open the gates and drive straight to Yin Ziqi's position, where they cut down officers and ripped out enemy banners.

sentences.zh: 有大酋被甲，引拓羯千騎麾幟乘城招巡。

translations.literal: A great chieftain in armor, leading a thousand Tuojie horsemen with banners flying, rode up onto the wall to summon Xun.
translations.idiomatic: A great chieftain in armor, at the head of a thousand Tuojie cavalry with banners flying, rode up onto the wall and called for Zhang Xun.

sentences.zh: 巡陰縋勇士數十人隍中，持鉤、陌刀、強弩，約曰：「聞鼓聲而奮。」

translations.literal: Xun secretly lowered several dozen brave men into the moat, armed with hooks, mo dao, and powerful crossbows, and arranged with them, "When you hear the drum, rise up.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun secretly lowered several dozen picked warriors into the moat with hooks, mo dao, and heavy crossbows, and told them, "At the sound of the drum, strike.

sentences.zh: 酋恃眾不為備，城上噪，伏發禽之，弩註矢外向，救兵不能前。

translations.literal: The chieftain, trusting in his numbers, made no preparations; there was an uproar on the wall, the ambush sprang up and seized him, and crossbows with arrows trained outward kept relief troops from advancing.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftain, confident in his numbers, took no precautions. A clamor rose on the wall, the hidden men sprang up and seized him, and crossbows with arrows aimed outward kept his rescuers from coming near.

sentences.zh: 俄而縋士復登陴，賊皆愕眙，乃按甲不出。

translations.literal: Before long the lowered men climbed back onto the battlements; the rebels all stared in shock, then held their armor and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the men in the moat were back on the battlements. The rebels stood stunned, then kept their armor on and would not venture out.

sentences.zh: 巡欲射子琦，莫能辨，因剡蒿為矢，中者喜，謂巡矢盡，走白子琦，乃得其狀。

translations.literal: Xun wished to shoot Ziqi but could not pick him out; so he carved reeds into arrows. Those struck rejoiced, thinking Xun's arrows were spent, and ran to tell Ziqi—thus learning his appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun wanted to shoot Yin Ziqi but could not tell which man he was. He carved reeds into arrow shafts. Those who were hit rejoiced, thinking his quiver was empty, and ran to tell Ziqi—thus revealing what he looked like.

sentences.zh: 使霽雲射，一發中左目，賊還。

translations.literal: He had Jiyun shoot; with one shot he hit the left eye, and the rebels withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He had Nan Jiyun take the shot. One arrow struck Yin Ziqi's left eye, and the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 七月，復圍城。

translations.literal: In the seventh month they again besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the rebels besieged the city once more.

sentences.zh: 初，睢陽谷六萬斛，可支一歲，而巨發其半餫濮陽、濟陰，遠固爭，不聽。

translations.literal: At first Suiyang had sixty thousand hu of grain, enough to last a year; but Ju sent half of it as provisions to Puyang and Jiyin, and though Yuan argued against it firmly, he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: At first Suiyang held sixty thousand hu of grain, enough to last a year. But Wang Ju sent half of it as rations to Puyang and Jiyin. Xu Yuan protested fiercely, but Wang Ju would not listen.

sentences.zh: 濟陰得糧即叛。

translations.literal: Jiyin, once it received the grain, immediately rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyin rebelled the moment it received the grain.

sentences.zh: 至是食盡，士日賦米一勺，龁木皮、煮紙而食，才千餘人，皆臒劣不能彀，救兵不至。

translations.literal: By then the food was gone. The soldiers were rationed one spoon of rice a day; they gnawed tree bark and boiled paper to eat. Only a little over a thousand men remained, all wasted and too weak to draw a bow, and no relief force came.
translations.idiomatic: By then the stores were exhausted. Each man received one spoon of rice a day. They gnawed bark and boiled paper to survive. Barely a thousand men were left, all gaunt and too weak to fight, and still no relief came.

sentences.zh: 賊知之，以雲沖傅堞，巡出鉤銘幹拄之，使不得進，篝火焚梯。

translations.literal: The rebels knew this. They pressed siege towers against the battlements; Xun extended hooked spears and poles to block them and keep them from advancing, and lit beacon fires to burn the ladders.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels knew their plight. They drove siege towers up against the walls. Zhang Xun thrust out hooked spears and poles to hold them back and set beacon fires to burn the ladders.

sentences.zh: 賊以鉤車、木馬進，巡輒破碎之。

translations.literal: The rebels advanced with hook carts and wooden-horse engines, and Xun each time smashed them apart.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels brought up hook carts and wooden-horse engines, and each time Zhang Xun smashed them to pieces.

sentences.zh: 賊服其機，不復攻，穿壕立柵以守。

translations.literal: The rebels admired his ingenuity and did not attack again; they dug moats and raised stockades to hold their ground.
translations.idiomatic: Impressed by his resourcefulness, the rebels stopped assaulting the walls and instead dug trenches and built palisades to keep the city bottled up.

sentences.zh: 巡士多餓死，存者皆痍傷氣乏。

translations.literal: Many of Xun's men starved to death; those who survived were all wounded and exhausted.
