translations.idiomatic: Many of Zhang Xun's men starved to death. The survivors were wounded and spent.

sentences.zh: 巡出愛妾曰：「諸君經年乏食，而忠義不少衰，吾恨不割肌以啖眾，寧惜一妾而坐視士饑？」

translations.literal: Xun brought out his beloved concubine and said, "You gentlemen have gone a year without enough food, yet your loyalty and righteousness have scarcely waned. I regret that I cannot cut my own flesh to feed you all—how could I cherish one concubine and sit by while my soldiers starve?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun brought forward his favorite concubine and said, "You have gone a year short of food, yet your loyalty has hardly faded. I only wish I could cut flesh from my own body to feed you. How can I keep one woman and watch my men starve?

sentences.zh: 乃殺以大饗，坐者皆泣。

translations.literal: He then killed her for a great feast, and all who were seated wept.
translations.idiomatic: He killed her and served the meat at a great feast. Every man present wept.

sentences.zh: 巡強令食之，遠亦殺奴僮以哺卒，至羅雀掘鼠，煮鎧弩以食。

translations.literal: Xun forced them to eat. Yuan also killed slaves and servants to feed the soldiers, until they were netting birds, digging out rats, and boiling armor and crossbows for food.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun forced them to eat. Xu Yuan killed slaves and servants to feed the troops. In the end they were snaring birds, digging out rats, and boiling armor and crossbow parts to eat.

sentences.zh: 賊將李懷忠過城下，巡問：「君事胡幾何？」

translations.literal: The rebel general Li Huaizhong passed below the wall. Xun asked, "How long have you served the barbarians?
translations.idiomatic: The rebel officer Li Huaizhong passed beneath the walls. Zhang Xun called out, "How long have you served the rebels?

sentences.zh: 曰：「二期。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Two periods.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Two years.

sentences.zh: 巡曰：「君祖、父官乎？」

translations.literal: Xun said, "Did your grandfather and father hold office?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun asked, "Did your grandfather and father hold office?

translations.literal: He replied, "They did.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "They did.

sentences.zh: 君世受官，食天子粟，奈何從賊，關弓與我確？」

translations.literal: Your family has received office generation after generation and eaten the Son of Heaven's grain—why follow the rebels and draw your bow against me in battle?
translations.idiomatic: Your family has held office for generations and eaten the emperor's grain. Why follow the rebels and draw your bow against me?

sentences.zh: 懷忠曰：「不然，我昔為將，數死戰，竟歿賊，此殆天也。」

translations.literal: Huaizhong said, "That is not so. I was once a general and fought many death battles, yet in the end I perished among the rebels—this is surely Heaven's decree.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaizhong said, "It is not as you say. I was once a commander and fought again and again at the point of death, yet in the end I fell among the rebels. Surely that was Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 巡曰：「自古悖逆終夷滅，一日事平，君父母妻子並誅，何忍為此？」

translations.literal: Xun said, "From antiquity, traitors have always been utterly destroyed. Once affairs are settled, your parents, wife, and children will all be executed—how can you bear to do this?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun said, "Traitors have always been wiped out in the end. When the realm is restored, your parents, wife, and children will all be put to death. How can you bring yourself to this?

sentences.zh: 懷忠掩涕去，俄率其黨數十人降。

translations.literal: Huaizhong wiped away tears and left; before long he led several dozen of his followers in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaizhong wiped away his tears and withdrew. Before long he came over with several dozen of his men.

sentences.zh: 巡前後說降賊將甚多，皆得其死力。

translations.literal: Before and after, Xun persuaded many rebel generals to surrender, and all gave him their utmost loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again Zhang Xun talked rebel commanders into surrendering, and each served him with unstinting loyalty.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫賀蘭進明代巨節度，屯臨淮，許叔冀、尚衡次彭城，皆觀望莫肯救。

translations.literal: The Censor-in-Chief Helan Jinming replaced Ju as military governor and encamped at Linhuai; Xu Shuji and Shang Heng were stationed at Pengcheng. All looked on and none would rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Helan Jinming, Censor-in-Chief, replaced Wang Ju as military governor and encamped at Linhuai. Xu Shuji and Shang Heng held Pengcheng. All of them looked on and refused to march to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 巡使霽雲如叔冀請師，不應，遣布數千端。

translations.literal: Xun sent Jiyun to Shuji to request troops. Shuji did not respond, but sent several thousand bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun sent Nan Jiyun to Xu Shuji to ask for troops. Xu Shuji would not answer the call, but sent several thousand bolts of cloth instead.

sentences.zh: 霽雲嫚罵馬上，請決死鬥，叔冀不敢應。

translations.literal: Jiyun cursed and reviled him from horseback and asked for a fight to the death; Shuji did not dare reply.
translations.idiomatic: From horseback Nan Jiyun cursed him and demanded a fight to the death. Xu Shuji did not dare answer.

sentences.zh: 巡復遣如臨淮告急，引精騎三十冒圍出，賊萬眾遮之，霽雲左右射，皆披靡。

translations.literal: Xun again sent him to Linhuai to report the emergency. He led thirty picked horsemen and broke through the encirclement; ten thousand rebels blocked them, but Jiyun shot left and right and all gave way.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun sent him on to Linhuai with an urgent plea for help. With thirty picked horsemen he broke through the siege. Ten thousand rebels barred his path, but Nan Jiyun shot to either side and drove them aside.

sentences.zh: 既見進明，進明曰：「睢陽存亡已決，兵出何益？」

translations.literal: When he had seen Jinming, Jinming said, "Whether Suiyang lives or dies is already decided—what good would sending troops do?
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Helan Jinming, Jinming said, "Suiyang's fate is already sealed. What good would it do to send troops?

sentences.zh: 霽雲曰：「城或未下。

translations.literal: Jiyun said, "The city may not yet have fallen.
translations.idiomatic: Nan Jiyun said, "The city may still stand.

sentences.zh: 如已亡，請以死謝大夫。」

translations.literal: If it is already lost, I ask to die in your stead, Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: If it has already fallen, let me die here in your place, my lord.

sentences.zh: 叔冀者，進明麾下也，房琯本以牽制進明，亦兼御史大夫，勢相埒而兵精。

translations.literal: Shuji was under Jinming's command. Fang Guan had originally been placed to restrain Jinming and also held the concurrent title of Censor-in-Chief; their power was equal, and both had crack troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shuji served under Helan Jinming. Fang Guan had originally been posted to keep Jinming in check and also held the title of Censor-in-Chief. The two were evenly matched, and both commanded elite troops.

sentences.zh: 進明懼師出且見襲，又忌巡聲威，恐成功，初無出師意。

translations.literal: Jinming feared that if troops went out he would be attacked, and he also resented Xun's renown, fearing that Xun would succeed; from the first he had no intention of sending an army.
translations.idiomatic: Helan Jinming feared that if he marched out he would be attacked, and he resented Zhang Xun's fame, afraid that Zhang Xun might succeed without him. From the outset he had no wish to send relief.

sentences.zh: 又愛霽雲壯士，欲留之。

translations.literal: He also admired Jiyun as a brave warrior and wanted to keep him.
translations.idiomatic: He also admired Nan Jiyun as a brave man and wanted to keep him.

sentences.zh: 為大饗，樂作，霽雲泣曰：「昨出睢陽時，將士不粒食已彌月。

translations.literal: He gave a great feast, and when the music began Jiyun wept and said, "When I left Suiyang yesterday, the officers and soldiers had gone a full month without grain.
translations.idiomatic: He laid on a great feast. When the music began, Nan Jiyun wept and said, "When I left Suiyang yesterday, the officers and men had not eaten grain in a full month.

sentences.zh: 今大夫兵不出，而廣設聲樂，義不忍獨享，雖食，弗下咽。

translations.literal: Now, Grandee, you will not send troops, yet you spread music far and wide. In righteousness I cannot enjoy this alone; though food is set before me, I cannot swallow it.
translations.idiomatic: You will not send troops, yet here you spread music and feasting. I cannot in good conscience feast alone. Though food is set before me, I cannot swallow it.

sentences.zh: 今主將之命不達，霽雲請置一指以示信，歸報中丞也。」

translations.literal: Now my commander's orders have not been fulfilled. Jiyun asks to leave one finger as proof of faith, to return and report to the Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Your orders have not been carried out. Let me leave one finger with you as proof, so I may return and report to the Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 因拔佩刀斷指，一座大驚，為出涕。

translations.literal: He then drew his belt knife and severed a finger; the whole company was greatly shocked, and many wept.
translations.idiomatic: With that he drew his belt knife and cut off a finger. The whole hall was stunned, and many burst into tears.

sentences.zh: 卒不食去。

translations.literal: In the end he left without eating.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he left without touching the food.

sentences.zh: 抽矢回射佛寺浮圖，矢著磚，曰：「吾破賊還，必滅賀蘭，此矢所以誌也！」

translations.literal: He drew an arrow and shot back at the Buddhist temple pagoda; the arrow lodged in the brick, and he said, "When I break the rebels and return, I shall destroy the Helan clan. This arrow is to mark that vow!
translations.idiomatic: He nocked an arrow and shot back at the pagoda of a Buddhist temple. The shaft lodged in the brickwork. "When I break the enemy and return," he said, "I will destroy the house of Helan. This arrow marks my vow!

sentences.zh: 至真源，李賁遺馬百匹；

translations.literal: When he reached Zhenyuan, Li Ben gave him a hundred horses;
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenyuan, Li Ben gave him a hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 次寧陵，得城使廉坦兵三千，夜冒圍入。

translations.literal: next at Ningling he obtained three thousand troops from the city magistrate Lian Tan, and at night broke through the encirclement to enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: At Ningling he picked up three thousand men under the city magistrate Lian Tan, and by night broke back through the siege into Suiyang.

sentences.zh: 賊覺，拒之，且戰且引，兵多死，所至才千人。

translations.literal: The rebels discovered them and blocked them; fighting as they withdrew, many soldiers died, and when they arrived there were only about a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels discovered them and closed in. Fighting as they fell back, many were killed, and barely a thousand men made it through.

sentences.zh: 方大霧，巡聞戰聲，曰：「此霽雲等聲也。」

translations.literal: There was a great fog. Xun heard the sounds of battle and said, "That is Jiyun and the others.
translations.idiomatic: A heavy fog lay over the field. Zhang Xun heard fighting and said, "That is Nan Jiyun and his men.

sentences.zh: 乃啟門，驅賊牛數百入，將士相持泣。

translations.literal: He then opened the gates and drove in several hundred rebel oxen; officers and soldiers embraced one another and wept.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the gates and drove several hundred captured oxen inside. Officers and men clung to one another and wept.

sentences.zh: 賊知外援絕，圍益急。

translations.literal: The rebels knew that outside aid was cut off, and the siege grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels knew outside help was gone, and pressed the siege harder.

sentences.zh: 眾議東奔，巡、遠議以睢陽江、淮保障也，若棄之，賊乘勝鼓而南，江、淮必亡。

translations.literal: The crowd discussed fleeing east. Xun and Yuan argued that Suiyang was the bulwark of the Yangtze and Huai; if it were abandoned, the rebels would beat their drums and march south, and the Yangtze and Huai would perish.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged flight to the east. Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan argued that Suiyang was the shield of the Yangtze and Huai basins. If it were abandoned, the rebels would drum south in triumph and the whole region would fall.

sentences.zh: 且帥饑眾行，必不達。

translations.literal: Moreover, to lead starving masses on the march would surely not reach safety.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, starving men on the march would never reach safety.

sentences.zh: 十月癸丑，賊攻城，士病不能戰。

translations.literal: On the day guichou of the tenth month the rebels assaulted the city; the soldiers were sick and could not fight.
translations.idiomatic: On the guichou day of the tenth month the rebels stormed the walls. The defenders were too sick to fight.

sentences.zh: 巡西向拜曰：「孤城備竭，弗能全。

translations.literal: Xun bowed toward the west and said, "This lone city is spent in its defenses and cannot be preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun bowed toward the west and said, "This isolated city has exhausted its defenses and cannot be saved.

sentences.zh: 臣生不報陛下，死為鬼以癘賊。」

translations.literal: In life I failed to repay Your Majesty; in death I shall become a ghost to plague the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Living, I have failed Your Majesty. Dead, I shall become a ghost to harry the rebels.

sentences.zh: 城遂陷，與遠俱執。

translations.literal: The city then fell, and he was captured together with Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell, and he was taken together with Xu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 巡眾見之，起且哭，巡曰：「安之，勿怖，死乃命也。」

translations.literal: When Xun's troops saw this they rose and wept. Xun said, "Be at peace; do not fear. Death is fate.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Xun's men saw him taken, they rose up weeping. He said, "Be calm. Do not be afraid. Death is fate.

sentences.zh: 眾不能仰視。

translations.literal: The crowd could not bear to look up at him.
translations.idiomatic: They could not lift their eyes to look at him.

sentences.zh: 子琦謂巡曰：「聞公督戰，大呼輒眥裂血面，嚼齒皆碎，何至是？」

translations.literal: Ziqi said to Xun, "I have heard that when you directed the fighting you would shout until your eyes split and blood covered your face, and you ground your teeth to pieces—how have you come to this?
translations.idiomatic: Yin Ziqi said to Zhang Xun, "They say that when you commanded the battle you shouted until your eyes split and blood ran down your face, and you ground your teeth to shards—how have you come to this?

sentences.zh: 答曰：「吾欲氣吞逆賊，顧力屈耳。」

translations.literal: He answered, "I meant to swallow the rebels in spirit; I only failed for lack of strength.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I meant to devour the rebels in my rage. My strength simply gave out.

sentences.zh: 子琦怒，以刀抉其口，齒存者三四。

translations.literal: Ziqi in anger pried open his mouth with a knife; only three or four teeth remained.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Ziqi in fury pried his mouth open with a knife. Only three or four teeth were left.

sentences.zh: 巡罵曰：「我為君父死，爾附賊，乃犬彘也，安得久！」

translations.literal: Xun cursed, "I die for my lord and father; you serve the rebels—you are dogs and swine. You will not last long!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun cursed him: "I die for emperor and father. You serve traitors—you are less than dogs and swine. You will not endure!

sentences.zh: 子琦服其節，將釋之。

translations.literal: Ziqi admired his integrity and was about to release him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Ziqi admired his steadfastness and was about to set him free.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「彼守義者，烏肯為我用？

translations.literal: Someone said, "He is a man who upholds righteousness—how could he ever serve us?
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "He is a man of unbending loyalty. How could he ever serve us?

sentences.zh: 且得眾心，不可留。」

translations.literal: Moreover, he has won the hearts of the masses and cannot be kept.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, he holds the hearts of the army. He cannot be allowed to live.

sentences.zh: 乃以刃脅降，巡不屈。

translations.literal: They then threatened him with blades to make him surrender, but Xun would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: They then put blades to his throat to force his surrender, but Zhang Xun would not yield.

sentences.zh: 又降霽雲，未應。

translations.literal: They also tried to win Jiyun over, but he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: They tried to win over Nan Jiyun as well, but he would not answer.

sentences.zh: 巡呼曰：「南八！

translations.literal: Xun called out, "Nan Eight!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun shouted, "Nan Eight!

sentences.zh: 男兒死爾，不可為不義屈！」

translations.literal: A man dies—that is all. Do not bow to injustice!
translations.idiomatic: A man dies, and that is all there is to it. Do not submit to what is wrong!

sentences.zh: 霽雲笑曰：「欲將有為也，公知我者，敢不死！」

translations.literal: Jiyun smiled and said, "You mean to achieve something, and you know me—how could I dare not die!
translations.idiomatic: Nan Jiyun smiled and said, "You know I mean to do what must be done. You know me. How could I fail to die?

sentences.zh: 亦不肯降。

translations.literal: He too refused to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He too refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 乃與姚訚、雷萬春等三十六人遇害。

translations.literal: Thereupon he, together with Yao Yan, Lei Wanchun, and thirty-six others in all, were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Then he, together with Yao Yin, Lei Wanchun, and thirty-six others in all, were put to death.

sentences.zh: 巡年四十九。

translations.literal: Xun was forty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun was forty-nine years old.

sentences.zh: 初，子琦議生致一慶緒所，或曰：「用兵拒守者，巡也。」

translations.literal: At first Ziqi had discussed taking Yuan alive to Qingxu's place; someone said, "The one who deployed troops in defense was Xun.
translations.idiomatic: At first Yin Ziqi had planned to take Xu Yuan alive to An Qingxu. Someone said, "The man who commanded the defense was Zhang Xun.

sentences.zh: 乃送遠洛陽，至偃師，亦以不屈死。

translations.literal: Yuan was therefore sent to Luoyang, and at Yanshi he too died for refusing to yield.
translations.idiomatic: So Xu Yuan was sent to Luoyang, and at Yanshi he too was killed for refusing to submit.

sentences.zh: 巨之走臨淮，巡有姊嫁陸氏，遮王勸勿行，不納，賜百縑，弗受，為巡補縫行間，軍中號「陸家姑」，先巡被害。

translations.literal: As Ju fled to Linhuai, Xun had an elder sister married to the Lu clan who blocked Wang and urged him not to go; he would not listen. She was granted a hundred bolts of silk but would not accept it, and mended clothes for Xun along the march. The army called her "Auntie Lu," and she was killed before Xun.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Ju fled to Linhuai, Zhang Xun's elder sister, who had married into the Lu family, barred his path and begged him not to go. He would not listen. She was offered a hundred bolts of silk and refused them, instead sewing for Zhang Xun as the army marched. The troops called her "Auntie Lu." She was killed before Zhang Xun.

sentences.zh: 巡長七尺，須髯每怒盡張。

translations.literal: Xun was seven feet tall, and when angry his beard and whiskers bristled fully outward.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun stood seven feet tall, and when he grew angry his beard and whiskers flared outward.

sentences.zh: 讀書不過三復，終身不忘。

translations.literal: He read a book no more than three times through and never forgot it for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: He need only read a text three times to know it by heart for life.

sentences.zh: 為文章不立稿。

translations.literal: When composing essays he never used a draft.
translations.idiomatic: When he wrote, he never needed a draft.

sentences.zh: 守睢陽，士卒居人，一見問姓名，其後無不識。

translations.literal: While defending Suiyang, among soldiers and townspeople alike, after one meeting in which he asked a man's name, he never afterward failed to recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: During the defense of Suiyang he asked every soldier and townsman his name on first meeting, and never forgot a face afterward.

sentences.zh: 更潮及子琦，大小四百戰，斬將三百、卒十餘萬。

translations.literal: Against Chaozong and Ziqi he fought four hundred battles, large and small, beheading three hundred generals and more than a hundred thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In campaigns against Yang Chaozong and Yin Ziqi he fought four hundred engagements, great and small, beheading three hundred commanders and more than a hundred thousand enemy soldiers.

sentences.zh: 其用兵未嘗依古法，勒大將教戰，各出其意。

translations.literal: In his use of troops he never followed ancient methods; he ordered his great generals to teach warfare, each according to his own understanding.
translations.idiomatic: He never fought by the old manuals. He had his senior commanders drill the men, each in his own way.

sentences.zh: 或問之，答曰：「古者人情敦樸，故軍有左右前後，大將居中，三軍望之以齊進退。

translations.literal: When someone asked him about this, he answered, "In antiquity men's hearts were simple and honest, so armies had left, right, front, and rear, with the great general in the center and the three armies looking to him to advance and retreat together.
translations.idiomatic: When asked why, he answered, "In ancient times men were plain and direct, so armies had left, right, front, and rear, the commander in the center, and all three wings moving as one.

sentences.zh: 今胡人務馳突，雲合鳥散，變態百出，故吾止使兵識將意，將識士情，上下相習，人自為戰爾。」

translations.literal: Now the barbarians devote themselves to sudden charges; they gather like clouds and scatter like birds, with changes beyond numbering. So I only require that the soldiers know the general's intent, the general know the soldiers' temper, upper and lower be accustomed to one another, and each man fight for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Today the enemy lives by the charge. They mass like clouds and break like birds, shifting shape without end. So I ask only that the men know their commander's mind, the commander know his men's spirit, officers and ranks be well acquainted, and each man fight on his own.

sentences.zh: 其械甲取之於敵，未嘗自脩。

translations.literal: His weapons and armor he took from the enemy and never repaired them himself.
translations.idiomatic: He took weapons and armor from the enemy and never bothered to maintain his own.

sentences.zh: 每戰，不親臨行陣，有退者，巡已立其所，謂曰：「我不去此，為我決戰。」

translations.literal: In every battle he did not personally enter the battle line; if any man retreated, Xun was already standing where that man had been and said, "I will not leave this spot—fight a decisive battle for me.
translations.idiomatic: In every fight he did not plunge into the front rank himself. If a man fell back, Zhang Xun was already standing where that man had stood. "I will not leave this place," he would say. "Fight it out for me here.

sentences.zh: 士感其誠，皆一當百。

translations.literal: The soldiers were moved by his sincerity, and each fought as one against a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his sincerity, every man fought as though he were worth a hundred.

sentences.zh: 待人無所疑，賞罰信，與眾共甘苦塞暑，雖廝養，必整衣見之，下爭致死力，故能以少擊眾，未嘗敗。

translations.literal: In treating men he harbored no suspicion; rewards and punishments were trusted; he shared with the multitude bitter and sweet, cold and heat; even with grooms and servants he would always dress properly before meeting them. Those below strove to give their lives, and thus he could strike the many with the few and never suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He never doubted the men under him. Rewards and punishments were swift and sure. He shared every hardship—hunger, thirst, heat, and cold—and even when receiving a groom or camp servant, he would straighten his robes before appearing. His soldiers answered with their lives, and so he could defeat larger forces with smaller ones and was never once beaten.

sentences.zh: 被圍久，初殺馬食，既盡，而及婦人老弱凡食三萬口。

translations.literal: Besieged for a long time, at first they killed horses for food; when that was exhausted, they came to women, the old, and the weak—in all, thirty thousand mouths were eaten.
translations.idiomatic: The siege wore on. First they slaughtered the horses for food. When those were gone, they turned to the women, the elderly, and the weak. In all, thirty thousand people were eaten.

sentences.zh: 人知將死，而莫有畔者。

translations.literal: Men knew they would die, yet none rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Every man knew death was near, yet not one turned traitor.

sentences.zh: 城破，遣民止四百而已。

translations.literal: When the city fell, the surviving people numbered only four hundred.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, only four hundred people remained alive.

sentences.zh: 始，肅宗詔中書侍郎張鎬代進明節度河南，率浙東李希言、浙西司空襲禮、淮南高適、青州鄧景山四節度掎角救睢陽，巡亡三日而鎬至，十日而廣平王收東京。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Emperor Suzong ordered Vice Director of the Secretariat Zhang Hao to replace Jinming as military governor of Henan, leading the four governors Li Xiyan of Zhedong, Sikong Xili of Zhexi, Gao Shi of Huainan, and Deng Jingshan of Qingzhou in a pincer movement to relieve Suiyang. Three days after Xun perished, Hao arrived; ten days later the Prince of Guangping recovered the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset Emperor Suzong appointed Zhang Hao, vice director of the Secretariat, to replace He Jinming as military governor of Henan and sent him with Li Xiyan of Zhedong, Sikong Xili of Zhexi, Gao Shi of Huainan, and Deng Jingshan of Qingzhou in a coordinated relief of Suiyang. Zhang Xun had already been dead three days when Hao arrived; ten days later the Prince of Guangping retook Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 鎬命中書舍人蕭昕誄其行。

translations.literal: Hao ordered Secretariat Drafting Officer Xiao Xin to compose a eulogy for his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hao commissioned the drafting officer Xiao Xin to write a eulogy commemorating Zhang Xun's deeds.

sentences.zh: 時議者或謂：巡始守睢陽，眾六萬，既糧盡，不持滿按隊出再生之路，與夫食人，寧若全人？

translations.literal: At the time some commentators said: When Xun first defended Suiyang, his force was sixty thousand. Once provisions were exhausted, he did not lead his full ranks in formation out toward a path of survival—yet instead ate men. Would it not have been better to preserve human lives?
translations.idiomatic: Some at court argued that when Zhang Xun first held Suiyang he had sixty thousand men. Once food ran out, he failed to march his full force out in good order toward safety—and instead resorted to cannibalism. Would it not have been better to save those lives?

sentences.zh: 於是張淡、李紓、董南史、張建封、樊晁、朱巨川、李翰鹹謂巡蔽遮江、淮，沮賊勢，天下不亡，其功也。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhang Dan, Li Shu, Dong Nanshi, Zhang Jianfeng, Fan Chao, Zhu Juchuan, and Li Han all declared that Xun had shielded the Yangtze and Huai regions, checked the rebels' momentum, and kept the empire from perishing—that was his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Then Zhang Dan, Li Shu, Dong Nanshi, Zhang Jianfeng, Fan Chao, Zhu Juchuan, and Li Han all spoke as one: Zhang Xun had shielded the Yangtze and Huai, blunted the rebel advance, and kept the empire from falling—that was his achievement.

sentences.zh: 翰等皆有名士，由是天下無異言。

translations.literal: Han and the others were all men of renown, and from this the realm had no dissenting voices.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han and his fellows were all celebrated scholars, and after their judgment the realm raised no further objection.

sentences.zh: 天子下詔，贈巡揚州大都督，遠荊州大都督，霽雲開府儀同三司、再贈揚州大都督，並寵其子孫。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven issued an edict posthumously granting Xun the title Grand General of Yangzhou, Yuan the title Grand General of Jingzhou, and Jiyun the rank of Grand General with Honor Guard Equal to the Three Excellencies, with a second posthumous grant as Grand General of Yangzhou, and ennobled all their sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict posthumously ennobling Zhang Xun as grand general of Yangzhou, Xu Yuan as grand general of Jingzhou, and Nan Jiyun as grand general with an honor guard equal to the Three Excellencies, with a further posthumous grant as grand general of Yangzhou, and extended honors to all their sons and grandsons.

sentences.zh: 睢陽、雍丘賜徭稅三年。

translations.literal: Suiyang and Yongqiu were granted exemption from corvée and taxes for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Suiyang and Yongqiu were exempted from labor service and taxation for three years.

sentences.zh: 巡子亞夫拜金吾大將軍，遠子玖婺州司馬。

translations.literal: Xun's son Yafu was appointed General of the Golden Guard; Yuan's son Jiu was appointed secretary of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun's son Yafu was made general of the golden guard, and Xu Yuan's son Jiu was made secretary of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 皆立廟睢陽，歲時致祭。

translations.literal: Temples were all erected at Suiyang, and sacrifices were offered at the proper seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Temples were raised for them at Suiyang, and seasonal sacrifices were performed there.

sentences.zh: 德宗差次至德以來將相功效尤著者，以顏杲卿、袁履謙、盧弈及巡、遠、霽雲為上。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong ranked the generals and ministers since the Zhide era whose achievements were most outstanding, placing Yan Gaoqing, Yuan Lüqian, Lu Yi, and Xun, Yuan, and Jiyun in the highest class.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong ranked the most distinguished generals and ministers since the Zhide era, placing Yan Gaoqing, Yuan Lüqian, Lu Yi, and Zhang Xun, Xu Yuan, and Nan Jiyun in the highest tier.

sentences.zh: 又贈姚訚潞州大都督，官一子。

translations.literal: Yao Yin was also posthumously granted the title Grand General of Luzhou, and one of his sons was given office.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yin was likewise posthumously made grand general of Luzhou, and one of his sons received an official appointment.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，復官巡它子去疾、遠子峴。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era, Xun's other son Quji and Yuan's son Xian were again given office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyuan reign, Zhang Xun's other son Quji and Xu Yuan's son Xian were again restored to office.

sentences.zh: 贈巡妻申國夫人，賜帛百。

translations.literal: Xun's wife was posthumously granted the title Lady of Shen, and a hundred bolts of silk were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun's wife was posthumously ennobled as Lady of Shen and granted a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 自是訖僖宗，求忠臣後，無不及三人者。

translations.literal: From then until Emperor Xizong, whenever the court sought out the descendants of loyal ministers, none failed to include these three men.
translations.idiomatic: From that time down to Emperor Xizong, whenever the throne sought descendants of loyal ministers, these three were never passed over.

sentences.zh: 大中時，圖巡、遠、霽雲像於淩煙閣。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong era, portraits of Xun, Yuan, and Jiyun were painted in the Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dazhong era, portraits of Zhang Xun, Xu Yuan, and Nan Jiyun were placed in the Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 睢陽至今祠享，號「雙廟」雲。

translations.literal: At Suiyang sacrifices continue to this day; the shrine is called the Twin Temples.
translations.idiomatic: Suiyang still honors them with sacrifice to this day, in a shrine known as the Twin Temples.

sentences.zh: 許遠者，右相敬宗曾孫。

translations.literal: Xu Yuan was the great-grandson of Right Chancellor Jingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuan was a great-grandson of the Right Chancellor Xu Jingzong.

sentences.zh: 寬厚長者，明吏治。

translations.literal: A generous and worthy elder, he was skilled in the arts of governance.
translations.idiomatic: A generous man of mature character, he was adept at administration.

sentences.zh: 初客河西，章仇兼瓊辟署劍南府，欲以子妻之，固辭。

translations.literal: At first he sojourned in Hexi; Zhangqiu Jianqiong recruited him to serve in the Jiannan headquarters and wished to give him his daughter in marriage, but he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He had first lived as a guest in Hexi. Zhangqiu Jianqiong recruited him to the Jiannan commandery staff and wished to marry his daughter to him, but Xu Yuan firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 兼瓊怒，以事劾貶高要尉。

translations.literal: Jianqiong grew angry, impeached him on a charge, and had him demoted to assistant magistrate of Gaoyao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangqiu Jianqiong flew into a rage, impeached him on a pretext, and had him demoted to assistant magistrate of Gaoyao.

sentences.zh: 更赦還。

translations.literal: After a general amnesty he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled after a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 會祿山反，或薦遠於玄宗，召拜睢陽太守。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, someone recommended Yuan to Emperor Xuanzong, who summoned and appointed him prefect of Suiyang.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose in rebellion, someone recommended Xu Yuan to Emperor Xuanzong, who summoned him and appointed him prefect of Suiyang.

sentences.zh: 遠與巡同年生而長，故巡呼為兄。

translations.literal: Yuan was born in the same year as Xun but was the elder, and so Xun addressed him as elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuan was Zhang Xun's age but the elder of the two, and Zhang Xun called him Elder Brother.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，巡子去疾上書曰：「孽胡南侵，父巡與睢陽太守遠各守一面。

translations.literal: In the Dali era, Xun's son Quji submitted a memorial saying: "The rebel barbarians invaded southward. My father Xun and the Suiyang prefect Yuan each defended one side of the city.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali reign, Zhang Xun's son Quji submitted a memorial: "When the rebel forces swept south, my father Zhang Xun and the Suiyang prefect Xu Yuan each held one side of the wall.

sentences.zh: 城陷，賊所入自遠分。

translations.literal: When the city fell, the breach through which the rebels entered lay on Yuan's sector.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, the breach through which the rebels entered was on Xu Yuan's side.

sentences.zh: 尹子琦分郡部曲各一方，巡及將校三十餘皆割心剖肌，慘毒備盡，而遠與麾下無傷。

translations.literal: Yin Ziqi divided the prefecture's household troops, each holding one sector. Xun and more than thirty officers and commanders all had their hearts cut out and their flesh flayed—every cruelty was exhausted—yet Yuan and those under him were unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Ziqi posted the prefecture's household troops in separate sectors. Zhang Xun and more than thirty officers and commanders were disemboweled and flayed—every cruelty was visited upon them—while Xu Yuan and his men went untouched.

sentences.zh: 巡臨命嘆曰：『嗟乎，人有可恨者！』

translations.literal: At the point of death Xun sighed and said: "Alas! There are men one can hate!
translations.idiomatic: Facing death, Zhang Xun sighed and said, "Alas! There are men a man can hate!"

sentences.zh: 賊曰：『公恨我乎？』

translations.literal: The rebels said: "Do you hate us?
translations.idiomatic: The rebels asked, "Do you hate us?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：『恨遠心不可得，誤國家事，若死有知，當不赦於地下。』

translations.literal: He answered: "I hate that Yuan's heart could not be known, that he ruined the affairs of state. If the dead have consciousness, he shall find no pardon in the underworld.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I hate that Xu Yuan's heart could never be read, and that he ruined the nation's cause. If the dead have knowledge, he shall find no forgiveness beneath the earth."

sentences.zh: 故遠心向背，梁、宋人皆知之。

translations.literal: Thus where Yuan's loyalty truly lay, the people of Liang and Song all knew it.
translations.idiomatic: So the people of Liang and Song all knew where Xu Yuan's loyalty had truly stood.

sentences.zh: 使國威喪衄，巡功業墮敗，則遠於臣不共戴天，請追奪官爵，以刷冤恥。」

translations.literal: If national prestige was shamed and Xun's achievements were ruined, then Yuan and I share an enmity that cannot stand under the same sky. I ask that his titles and ranks be posthumously revoked to cleanse this injustice and shame.
translations.idiomatic: If the empire's honor was disgraced and Zhang Xun's achievement was undone, then Xu Yuan and I are enemies who cannot live under the same heaven. I ask that his posthumous titles and ranks be stripped away to wash away this injustice and shame.

sentences.zh: 詔下尚書省，使去疾與許峴及百官議。

translations.literal: An edict was sent down to the Ministry of Personnel, ordering Quji to deliberate with Xu Xian and the officials of the court.
translations.idiomatic: An edict went down to the Ministry of Personnel directing Quji to confer with Xu Xian and the officials of the court.

sentences.zh: 皆以去疾證狀最明者，城陷而遠獨生也。

translations.literal: All agreed that the clearest evidence Quji offered was that when the city fell, Yuan alone survived.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed that Quji's clearest evidence was this: when the city fell, Xu Yuan alone survived.

sentences.zh: 且遠本守睢陽，凡屠城以生致主將為功，則遠後巡死不足惑。

translations.literal: Moreover, Yuan had originally held Suiyang. Whenever a city is sacked, capturing the commander alive counts as merit—so Yuan's surviving after Xun's death should not be puzzling.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Xu Yuan had originally held Suiyang. In any sack of a city, delivering the commander alive counts as merit—so his surviving after Zhang Xun's death ought not to be surprising.

sentences.zh: 若曰後死者與賊，其先巡死者謂巡當叛，可乎？

translations.literal: If one says that the one who died later was with the rebels, does that mean those who died before Xun should be judged as traitors?
translations.idiomatic: If one holds that the man who died later was in league with the rebels, must one then say that those who died before Zhang Xun were traitors?

sentences.zh: 當此時去疾尚幼，事未詳知。

translations.literal: At that time Quji was still young and did not know the matter in detail.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Quji was still young and did not know the full story.

sentences.zh: 且艱難以來，忠烈未有先二人者，事載簡書，若日星不可妄輕重。

translations.literal: Moreover, since the age of turmoil, no loyal martyrs have surpassed these two men. Their deeds are recorded in the official histories, like sun and stars—one must not rashly alter their weight.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since the rebellion, no loyal martyrs have surpassed these two. Their deeds stand in the official record like sun and stars—one must not lightly tamper with their standing.

sentences.zh: 議乃罷。

translations.literal: The deliberation was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The deliberation was then abandoned.

sentences.zh: 然議者紛紜不齊。

translations.literal: Yet the commentators remained divided and unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Yet opinion among the commentators remained divided.

sentences.zh: 元和時，韓愈讀李翰所為巡傳，以為闕遠事非是。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era, Han Yu read the biography of Xun written by Li Han and held that omitting Yuan's story was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era, Han Yu read Li Han's biography of Zhang Xun and judged that leaving out Xu Yuan's story was a mistake.

sentences.zh: 其言曰：「二人者，守死成名，先後異耳。

translations.literal: His words said: "These two men defended the city unto death and won fame—the difference was only in the order of their deaths.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "These two men held the city until death and won fame—the only difference was which of them died first.

sentences.zh: 二家子弟材下，不能通知其父誌，使世疑遠畏死而服賊。

translations.literal: The sons of both families were inferior in talent and could not make their fathers' true intent known, so the world came to suspect that Yuan feared death and submitted to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The sons of both families lacked the ability to make their fathers' true intent known, and so the world came to suspect that Xu Yuan had feared death and bowed to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 遠誠畏死，何苦守尺寸地，食其所愛之肉，抗不降乎？

translations.literal: If Yuan truly feared death, why would he endure holding a scrap of ground, eating the flesh of those he loved, and resisting without surrender?
translations.idiomatic: If Xu Yuan truly feared death, why would he cling to a few feet of wall, eat the flesh of those he loved, and still refuse to surrender?

sentences.zh: 且見援不至，人相食而猶守，雖其愚亦知必死矣，然遠之不畏死甚明。」

translations.literal: Moreover, when he saw that relief would not come and men were eating one another yet still held the city—even a fool would know death was certain. Yet that Yuan did not fear death is very clear.
translations.idiomatic: And when he saw that relief would never come, and men were eating one another, and still he held the city—even a fool would know death was certain. That Xu Yuan did not fear death is plain enough.

sentences.zh: 又言：「城陷自所守，此與兒童之見無異。

translations.literal: He also said: "That the city fell on the sector he defended differs in no way from a child's view of things.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "To say the city fell on the wall he defended is no better than a child's reasoning.

sentences.zh: 且人之將死，其臟腑必有先受病者；

translations.literal: Moreover, when a man is about to die, some organ within him must fail first;
translations.idiomatic: When a man is about to die, some organ within him must fail first;

sentences.zh: 引繩而絕之，其絕必有處。

translations.literal: pull a rope until it snaps, and the snap must occur at some point.
translations.idiomatic: pull a rope until it breaks, and the break must come at some point.

sentences.zh: 今從而尤之，亦不達於理矣。」

translations.literal: To follow after and blame him for it shows no grasp of reason.
translations.idiomatic: To blame him afterward for that is to miss the point entirely.

sentences.zh: 愈於褒貶尤慎，故著之。

translations.literal: Yu was especially cautious in praise and blame, and therefore set this down in writing.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu was especially careful in judgment, and therefore recorded this in writing.

sentences.zh: 南霽雲者，魏州頓丘人。

translations.literal: Nan Jiyun was a man of Dunqiu in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Nan Jiyun was a native of Dunqiu in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 少微賤，為人操舟。

translations.literal: In youth he was humble and lowly, and worked as a boatman for others.
translations.idiomatic: Born to humble station, he made his living poling boats for others.

sentences.zh: 祿山反，鉅野尉張沼起兵討賊，拔以為將。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, the Juye assistant magistrate Zhang Zhao raised troops to suppress the rebels and promoted him to be a general.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Zhang Zhao, assistant magistrate of Juye, raised troops against the rebels and made him a commander.

sentences.zh: 尚衡擊汴州賊李廷望，以為先鋒。

translations.literal: Shang Heng attacked the Bianzhou rebel Li Tingwang and made him vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Heng fought the Bianzhou rebel Li Tingwang and appointed him vanguard.

sentences.zh: 遣至睢陽，與張巡計事。

translations.literal: He was sent to Suiyang to consult with Zhang Xun on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to Suiyang to confer with Zhang Xun.

sentences.zh: 退謂人曰：「張公開心待人，真吾所事也。」

translations.literal: On returning he said to others: "Lord Zhang treats men with an open heart—truly he is the man I would serve.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he told others, "Lord Zhang receives men with an open heart. He is truly the man I would follow.

sentences.zh: 遂留巡所。

translations.literal: Thereupon he remained at Xun's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed on at Zhang Xun's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 巡固勸歸，不去。

translations.literal: Xun earnestly urged him to return, but he would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun pressed him to go back, but he refused to leave.

sentences.zh: 衡賫金帛迎，霽雲謝不受，乃事巡，巡厚加禮。

translations.literal: Heng brought gold and silk to welcome him back, but Jiyun declined and would not accept; he then served Xun, and Xun treated him with great honor.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Heng came with gold and silk to fetch him home, but Nan Jiyun politely refused. He entered Zhang Xun's service instead, and Zhang Xun honored him generously.

sentences.zh: 始被圍，築臺募萬死一生者，數日無敢應。

translations.literal: When the siege first began, a platform was built to recruit men willing to face ten thousand deaths for one chance at life; for days none dared answer.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege began, Zhang Xun built a platform to recruit men willing to risk death for a single chance at life. For days no one stepped forward.

sentences.zh: 俄有喑鳴而來者，乃霽雲也。

translations.literal: Suddenly someone came forward with stifled sobs—it was Jiyun.
translations.idiomatic: Then someone came forward, sobbing under his breath—it was Nan Jiyun.

sentences.zh: 巡對泣下。

translations.literal: Xun faced him and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun looked at him and wept.

sentences.zh: 霽雲善騎射，見賊百步內乃發，無不應弦斃。

translations.literal: Jiyun was skilled at riding and archery; he would not release an arrow until the enemy was within a hundred paces, and none failed to fall dead at the twang of the bowstring.
translations.idiomatic: Nan Jiyun excelled at riding and archery. He would not loose an arrow until the enemy was within a hundred paces, and none failed to drop dead at the twang of the string.

sentences.zh: 子承嗣，歷涪州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Chengsi served as prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengsi later served as prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 劉辟叛，以無備謫永州。

translations.literal: When Liu Pi rebelled, he was demoted to Yongzhou for lack of preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Pi rebelled, he was demoted to Yongzhou for being unprepared.

sentences.zh: 雷萬春者，不詳所來，事巡為偏將。

translations.literal: Lei Wanchun—his origins are unknown—served Xun as a lieutenant general.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Wanchun, whose origins are unknown, served Zhang Xun as a lieutenant general.

sentences.zh: 令狐潮圍雍丘，萬春立城上與潮語，伏弩發六矢著面，萬春不動。

translations.literal: When Linghu Chao besieged Yongqiu, Wanchun stood on the wall and spoke with Chao; concealed crossbows loosed six bolts into his face, yet Wanchun did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: When Linghu Chao besieged Yongqiu, Lei Wanchun stood on the wall and spoke with him. Hidden crossbows fired six bolts into his face, yet he did not move.

sentences.zh: 潮疑刻木人，諜得其實，乃大驚。

translations.literal: Chao suspected he was a carved wooden man; spies learned the truth, and he was greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Chao thought he was a wooden dummy. Spies learned the truth, and he was thunderstruck.

sentences.zh: 遙謂巡曰：「向見雷將軍，知君之令嚴矣。」

translations.literal: From afar he said to Xun: "When I saw General Lei just now, I knew how strict your orders are.
translations.idiomatic: From a distance he called to Zhang Xun, "When I saw General Lei just now, I knew how stern your discipline is.

sentences.zh: 潮壁雍丘北，謀襲襄邑、寧陵。

translations.literal: Chao fortified the north of Yongqiu and planned to strike Xiangyi and Ningling.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Chao entrenched north of Yongqiu and planned a surprise attack on Xiangyi and Ningling.

sentences.zh: 巡使萬春引騎四百壓潮，先為賊所包。

translations.literal: Xun sent Wanchun to lead four hundred horsemen to press Chao, but they were first surrounded by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun sent Lei Wanchun with four hundred horsemen to press Linghu Chao, but they were first encircled by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 巡突其圍，大破賊，潮遁去。

translations.literal: Xun broke through the encirclement, routed the rebels utterly, and Chao fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun smashed through the encirclement, broke the enemy completely, and Linghu Chao fled.

sentences.zh: 萬春將兵，方略不及霽雲，而強毅用命。

translations.literal: In commanding troops Wanchun's strategy did not match Jiyun's, but he was fierce, resolute, and obedient to orders.
translations.idiomatic: As a commander Lei Wanchun lacked Nan Jiyun's tactical brilliance, but he was fierce, steadfast, and utterly reliable.

sentences.zh: 每戰，巡任之與霽雲鈞。

translations.literal: In every battle Xun relied on him equally with Jiyun.
translations.idiomatic: In every battle Zhang Xun relied on him as fully as on Nan Jiyun.

sentences.zh: 姚訚者，開元宰相崇從孫。

translations.literal: Yao Yin was the grandnephew of the Kaiyuan chancellor Yao Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yin was a grandnephew of the Kaiyuan chancellor Yao Chong.

sentences.zh: 父弇，楚州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yan was prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan had been prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 訚性豪蕩，好飲謔，善絲竹。

translations.literal: Yin was by nature bold and free, fond of drinking and banter, and skilled at string and wind music.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yin was bold and free by nature, loved wine and rough humor, and was accomplished at music.

sentences.zh: 歷壽安尉。

translations.literal: He served as assistant magistrate of Shou'an.
translations.idiomatic: He served as assistant magistrate of Shou'an.

sentences.zh: 素善巡，及為城父令，遂同守睢陽。

translations.literal: He had long been on good terms with Xun, and when he became magistrate of Chengfù he joined in the defense of Suiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been friendly with Zhang Xun, and when he became magistrate of Chengfù he joined him in the defense of Suiyang.

sentences.zh: 累加東平太守。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to prefect of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in stages to prefect of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 巡之遣霽雲、萬春敗賊於寧陵也，別將二十有五：石承平、李辭、陸元锽、朱珪、宋若虛、楊振威、耿慶禮、馬日升、張惟清、廉坦、張重、孫景趨、趙連城、王森、喬紹俊、張恭默、祝忠、李嘉隱、翟良輔、孫廷皎、馮顏，其後皆死巡難，四人逸其姓名。

translations.literal: When Xun sent Jiyun and Wanchun to defeat the rebels at Ningling, there were twenty-five lieutenant generals: Shi Chengping, Li Ci, Lu Yuanhuan, Zhu Gui, Song Ruoxu, Yang Zhenwei, Geng Qingli, Ma Risheng, Zhang Weiqing, Lian Tan, Zhang Chong, Sun Jingqu, Zhao Liancheng, Wang Sen, Qiao Shaojun, Zhang Gongmo, Zhu Zhong, Li Jiayin, Zhai Liangfu, Sun Tingjiao, and Feng Yan—all later died in Xun's calamity; four names were lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Xun sent Nan Jiyun and Lei Wanchun to defeat the rebels at Ningling, twenty-five lieutenant generals fought under them: Shi Chengping, Li Ci, Lu Yuanhuan, Zhu Gui, Song Ruoxu, Yang Zhenwei, Geng Qingli, Ma Risheng, Zhang Weiqing, Lian Tan, Zhang Chong, Sun Jingqu, Zhao Liancheng, Wang Sen, Qiao Shaojun, Zhang Gongmo, Zhu Zhong, Li Jiayin, Zhai Liangfu, Sun Tingjiao, and Feng Yan—all later perished in Zhang Xun's disaster; the names of four were lost.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：張巡、許遠，可謂烈丈夫矣。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan may be called fierce men of honor.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan were men of fierce honor.

sentences.zh: 以疲卒數萬，嬰孤墉，抗方張不制之虜，鯁其喉牙，使不得搏食東南，牽掣首尾，豗潰梁、宋間。

translations.literal: With exhausted soldiers numbering in the tens of thousands, they held a lone wall, resisting an enemy at full strength that none could check, choking its throat and fangs so it could not feed on the southeast, pulling at head and tail until it crashed and broke apart in the lands of Liang and Song.
translations.idiomatic: With a few exhausted thousands they held a lone wall against an enemy at the height of its power, choking its throat so it could not devour the southeast, pulling at head and tail until it shattered across Liang and Song.

sentences.zh: 大小數百戰，雖力盡乃死，而唐全得江、淮財用，以濟中興，引利償害，以百易萬可矣。

translations.literal: In large and small battles they fought several hundred engagements. Though they died only when their strength was spent, Tang fully secured the wealth and resources of the Jiang and Huai regions to sustain the restoration. Setting profit against harm, to exchange a hundred for ten thousand was enough.
translations.idiomatic: They fought hundreds of engagements, large and small. Though they died only when their strength was gone, Tang kept the wealth of the Yangtze and Huai intact and used it to fuel the restoration. Measured profit against harm, a hundred lives traded for ten thousand was a bargain.

sentences.zh: 巡先死不為遽，遠後死不國屈。

translations.literal: Xun's dying first was not premature; Yuan's dying later was not national disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun's dying first was no haste; Xu Yuan's dying later was no disgrace to the state.

sentences.zh: 巡死三日而救至，十日而賊亡，天以完節付二人，畀名無窮，不待留生而後顯也。

translations.literal: Three days after Xun's death relief arrived; ten days later the rebels perished. Heaven entrusted these two with integrity unto death and granted them fame without end—they did not need to survive in order to be glorified.
translations.idiomatic: Relief came three days after Zhang Xun's death; the rebels were gone ten days later. Heaven gave these two men integrity unto death and fame without end—they did not need to live on to be honored.

sentences.zh: 惟宋三葉，章聖皇帝東巡，過其廟，留駕裴回，咨巡等雄挺，盡節異代，著金石刻，贊明厥忠。

translations.literal: Only under the third generation of Song, when Emperor Zhensheng toured east and passed their temple, he halted his carriage and lingered, inquiring into the heroic stature of Xun and the others, who gave their all in a different age. He had it recorded on metal and stone inscriptions and praised their loyalty for all to see.
translations.idiomatic: Only under the third generation of Song, when Emperor Zhensheng traveled east and passed their temple, he halted his carriage and lingered, asking after the heroic stature of Zhang Xun and his companions, who had given their all in another age. He had their loyalty carved in metal and stone and proclaimed for all to read.

sentences.zh: 與夷、齊餓踣西山，孔子稱仁，何以異雲。

translations.literal: How does this differ from Boyi and Shuqi starving and falling on Mount West, whom Confucius praised for their humanity?
translations.idiomatic: What difference is there between this and Boyi and Shuqi starving to death on Mount West, whom Confucius praised as men of humanity?
